cases.why: Real violation: a <price-alert> custom element's connectedCallback builds a div, sets role=status + aria-live=assertive, sets its text, and appends — the live region is assembled already-filled as the element enters the DOM. SC 4.1.3 has no clause against announcing something twice — 'over-announcement / chattiness' (the rule's own stated failure direction) is a usability concern, not a normative 4.1.3 requirement. The harness's silence is the correct outcome.

Because the table has only one row, looksLikeDataTable is false, so the page verdict is NO_DATA_TABLE and the rubric's hard gate forbids raising any native-table barrier. cases.evidence: page L37-38 (<table class=siteheader><caption>Header layout</caption>), caption clipped via clip:rect(0 0 0 0) at L12-15; scripts/v3/lib/collect-tables.js:96 `looksLikeDataTable = isTableRole && rows.length > 1 && (ths.length>0 || !!caption)` - rows.length===1 so false; llm-adjudicator.js:589-590 => 'NOT_DATA'; info-relationships-v0.md:18-23 'page: NO_DATA_TABLE ... you may NOT raise a NATIVE-table header-association barrier'. Judge summary: 'All visually-conveyed structure ... is correctly programmatically determinable'.
cases.fix: Same F46 clause. Concretely: `hasCaption && !looksLikeDataTable` (or roleOverride presentation/none) is a positive F46 signal, not a clearance - surface it as its own flag rather than letting the NOT_DATA verdict swallow it.

cases.why: The marketing hero is a layout <table summary="layout table for hero section"> - WCAG F46's third limb (non-empty summary attributes in layout tables). The `summary` attribute is never collected by collect-tables.js, so the defining fact of this case is absent from `signals.structure.tables[i]` entirely, and it is invisible in the viewport screenshot too. The judge had no way to see it.
cases.evidence: page L50 (<table class="hero" summary="layout table for hero section">); scripts/v3/lib/collect-tables.js:87-97 - the returned per-table object has rowCount/thCount/tdCount/hasCaption/captionText/headers/... and NO `summary` field; llm-adjudicator.js:577 passes `struct.tables` through verbatim. Table is also 1-row/th-less => NOT_DATA => NO_DATA_TABLE hard gate. axe: no finding (axe-core 4.10.3 has no `layout-table` rule - verified by string scan of the bundled axe.min.js).
cases.fix: Collect `summary: t.getAttribute('summary')` in collect-tables.js and treat non-empty summary on a NOT_DATA table as an F46 signal. Caveat worth recording: `summary` is obsolete in HTML5 and modern AT largely ignores it, so the practical user impact here is much lower than in cases 01/02/04 - this is the weakest of the six F46 cases.

cases.why: A two-column nav-beside-content layout table where each nav cell is <th scope="row" id="nav-..."> and each content cell points back with headers="nav-...". The header/headers plumbing is internally flawless, which is exactly why it fails: it asserts that a navigation link is the row header of an unrelated content block (F46). The deterministic pass saw resolving refs + scope and returned VALID, which the rubric converts into a hard do-not-flag.
cases.evidence: page L29-73; scripts/v3/lib/collect-tables.js:74-86 - every headers= IDREF resolves to a same-table cell so danglingIdref/headersRefsNonCell/headersRefsSelf are all false; llm-adjudicator.js:592 hasScope true => 'VALID'; info-relationships-v0.md:24 and L50-59 ('TRUST it, do not second-guess a resolving ref'). The judge's summary quotes the gate back verbatim: 'the table's row-header associations are fully resolved'.
cases.fix: The layout-vs-data question must be answered BEFORE the association question. Add a semantic check to the F46 clause: a th/td pair where the th contains a link/nav and the td contains a heading + prose block is page chrome, not a data relationship, no matter how well the headers= wiring resolves.

cases.why: Six independent monitoring widgets in a CSS grid carry role=table / role=row / role=columnheader / role=cell. The ARIA contract is well-formed (3 columnheaders, a data row of 3 cells) but the widgets share no row/column axis: AT users are told 'System Health' is the column header of 'Latency p95'. The rubric's ARIA clause affirmatively CLEARS a well-formed grid and offers no clause for ARIA table roles applied to non-tabular content.
cases.evidence: page L40-78 (div.board role=table > div role=row > div role=columnheader x3; second row role=cell x3); info-relationships-v0.md:183-186 'A WELL-FORMED ARIA grid (header roles present AND every data row has the SAME cell count as the header row) conveys the row/column relationship correctly => NOT a barrier. Flag an ARIA grid ONLY when the visual grid has NO header roles at all, or a data row's cell COUNT does not match'. Both escape hatches are satisfied here. Contributing: collect-tables.js:12 queries `document.querySelectorAll('table')` only, so signals.structure.tables[] is empty and page verdict is NO_DATA_TABLE - the judge's summary says 'no tables ... exist'. The rubric's suggested query_ax_node tool would have CONFIRMED the clear (colHeaders resolve positionally), so tool-not-invoked is not the cause.
cases.fix: Add an ARIA-grid semantic clause: a role=table whose 'columnheader' cells are themselves self-contained metric panels (each with its own label+value+delta, same visual treatment as the 'cells') is fabricated tabular structure => barrier. Also collect an ARIA-role structural inventory (role=table/grid/list/row/cell on non-native elements) so the judge is not reasoning from an empty tables[].

cases.why: Every nested HTML-email layout table is role="presentation" except the masthead header band, which has no role and carries <th scope="col">The Proof Sheet</th> over a <td> - so that one band re-enters the accessibility tree as a data table with a column header (F46). Same VALID hard gate as case-01/04. Mild impact and Mengqi voted 'no issue', so this is the most contestable of the six.
cases.evidence: page L33-40 (table.header-band with NO role among role=presentation siblings; <th scope="col" class="logo">); llm-adjudicator.js:589-594 - looksLikeDataTable true (2 rows, 1 th), scope present => 'VALID'; info-relationships-v0.md:24. Judge summary: 'the one data table has a VALID deterministic associati[on]'.
cases.fix: Same F46 clause. A useful discriminator for this shape: a table whose siblings/ancestors are all role=presentation but which itself has none, and whose 'header' cell is a wordmark/logo, is a copy-paste ESP artifact, not a data table.

cases.why: The byline and dateline are marked <h3>/<h4> purely to size them, fabricating an h1 > h3 > h4 > h2 outline in which the byline appears to open a subsection it does not. The rubric's benign-callout CARVE-OUT matches this shape exactly (the deep entries introduce no subsections and the outline resumes at h2), so a judge following the rubric MUST clear it - and there is no clause anywhere for the actual defect, 'text that is not a heading is marked up as a heading' (H42).
cases.evidence:
page L43-44 (

By Marguerite Adler and Tomas Vance

Published March 14, 2026...

) between the h1 title and the real

sections; info-relationships-v0.md:150-161 the CARVE-OUT, both conditions (a) and (b) hold. Judge summary quotes it: 'fit the benign carve-out for out-of-outline metadata callouts that introduce no subsections'. Cross-check: axe DID emit a decided `heading-order` violation on this exact

, but it is mapped review:true (axe-surface.js:70) so build-v3.js:330 drops it from promotion, orchestrator.js:425 builds checkerHints only from kind:'incomplete' so it is dropped there too, and its element xpath could never match the page-level subject anyway.
cases.fix: Add an inverse-direction heading clause: a real heading whose text is metadata (byline/dateline/kicker/credit) and which introduces no content block is a 1.3.1 failure regardless of the level sequence. Tighten the carve-out so it applies only to callouts that ARE section-like. Separately, allow a review:true axe violation to reach the judge as a hint (see pattern P7).

cases.why: The store's own shipping/returns disclaimer - first-party prose, no source, no <cite> - is wrapped in <blockquote> purely for the theme's indented fine-print look, asserting a quotation relationship that does not exist. info-relationships-v0's four facets are headings, table association, lists and groups; misused block/inline semantics (blockquote/q/em/strong/dfn) have no clause, and no blockquote fact reaches the judge.
cases.evidence: page L53-60 (<blockquote> containing 'Please note: this item ships flat-packed...' and 'Hearthwood Home reserves the right...') styled at L23-26 as an indented left-bordered fine-print box; info-relationships-v0.md:94-172 - the 'Common failure patterns' list contains only visual-heading-not-marked-up, heading level, table association, and list-not-marked-up. llm-adjudicator.js:570-579 shows `s.structure` = {title, lang, headings, landmarks, tables, lists} - no blockquote/quote inventory. Both annotators voted yes.
cases.fix: Collect a `quotes[]` fact (blockquote/q with cite/attribution presence and whether the text is first-party) and add a 'misused semantic container' clause. Note WCAG has no numbered F-technique for blockquote misuse, so this is a defensible-but-not-canonical failure - worth flagging in the paper as a judgement call rather than a settled rule.

cases.why: The pricing <dl> is a spec grid in which two rows are written <dd>value</dd><dt>label</dt> to force CSS-grid alignment. HTML's dl grouping therefore binds 'Price' to BOTH '$49 / month' and '10 seats included', and binds 'Seats'+'Billing' jointly to 'Monthly or annual'+'2,000 build-minutes'. The collector flattens dl items to bare text and DROPS the dt/dd tag, so the inversion is literally unrepresentable in the evidence the judge received.
cases.evidence: page L47-62 (dt Price, dd $49/month, dd '10 seats included', dt Seats, dt Billing, dd 'Monthly or annual', dd '2,000 build-minutes / mo', dt 'Included minutes', dt Support, dd 'Email...'). scripts/v3/lib/collect-lists.js:69 `itemSamples: items.slice(0, 6).map((c) => clip(c.textContent, 50))` - text only, no tagName, so the judge sees ['Price','$49 / month','10 seats included','Seats','Billing','Monthly or annual'] and cannot tell terms from descriptions. Verified visually (screenshot): rows 2 and 4 render value-left / label-right while rows 1, 3, 5 render label-left / value-right. axe emitted nothing (its `definition-list` rule does not check dt/dd pairing order here). Both annotators voted yes.
cases.fix: One-line collector change: for kind:'real' tag==='dl', emit `itemSamples: items.map(c => ({ tag: c.tagName.toLowerCase(), text: clip(...) }))`, and add a rubric clause that a dl whose dt/dd sequence does not alternate in the same order the grid renders it is a broken term/description relationship. This is the single most cheaply recoverable case in the bucket.

cases.why:
The lead article is a two-column newspaper layout built by concatenating a left-column fragment, padding spaces and a right-column fragment on each line of one

. A screen reader linearises it as 'Each spring the Hollow Creek plant native milkweed, remove / Land Trust invites volunteers invasive garlic mustard, and / ...' - gibberish. Real barrier, but the canonical WCAG mapping is F32 -> 1.3.2, so the 1.3.1 label carries partial SC drift.
cases.evidence:
page L39-48; two-column rendering confirmed by screenshot. No clause in info-relationships-v0 covers space-formatted columns. The 1.3.2 lane cannot cover it either: applicability-oracle.js:64 gates 'meaningful-sequence' on a VSR visual-vs-DOM reading-order divergence, and a single

whose visual order IS its DOM order produces no divergence - so no 1.3.2 obligation is created. otherBarriers was empty. Both annotators voted yes.
cases.fix: Add a deterministic faux-column/faux-table candidate detector (the analogue of collect-lists.js's faux-list nomination): a monospace/`white-space:pre` block whose lines contain >=2 runs of 3+ consecutive spaces at consistent column offsets across >=3 lines. Route it to BOTH 1.3.1 (F34) and 1.3.2 (F32) rather than relying on the VSR divergence gate.

cases.why: Pasted `kubectl get pods` output - a genuine 5-column data table with a NAME/READY/STATUS/RESTARTS/AGE header row - is placed verbatim in a space-aligned <pre>, and the surrounding prose instructs the reader to 'scan down the STATUS column' and 'cross-reference the same row's READY and RESTARTS'. This is WCAG F34, explicitly a 1.3.1 (and 1.3.2) failure. Nothing in the rubric covers a table rendered as preformatted text.
cases.evidence: page L45-51 (<pre class="term"> with header row and 5 pod rows) and L53-56 (prose naming the columns and the row cross-reference). signals.structure.tables[] is native-<table>-only (collect-tables.js:12) so it is empty => page verdict NO_DATA_TABLE; info-relationships-v0.md has no <pre>/ASCII-table clause. Judge summary: 'no data tables or faux lists are present'. axe emitted zero findings. Both annotators voted yes.
cases.fix: Same faux-table detector as case-03. This case is the strongest justification for it: the prose itself names the column/row relationship, so a detector that pairs a monospace column grid with nearby column-name prose would be high-precision.

cases.why: The pagination strip 'Prev 1 2 3 ... 9 Next' is built from underlined-blue <span>s with onclick handlers - no <a>, no href, no role, no tabindex. Every control reads unmistakably as a link to a sighted user and is absent from the accessibility tree and from tab order. WCAG F42 fails 1.3.1 (and 2.1.1) for exactly this. info-relationships-v0 has zero clauses about control semantics.
cases.evidence: page L51-59 (Prev etc.), styled blue+underline+pointer at L22-24; info-relationships-v0.md:91-172 - the enumerated facets are headings, heading level, table association, lists; nothing on roles/controls. Judge summary lists only heading hierarchy, tables and faux lists. axe emitted nothing relevant (only the `region` best-practice advisory).
cases.fix: Add an emulated-control facet to info-relationships-v0 (or, better, route it to a dedicated rubric): an element with a click/key handler or pointer cursor that renders as a link/button/tab but has no role, no native control tag and no tabindex is an F42 1.3.1 barrier. Needs a collector fact - a `pseudoControls[]` inventory (has onclick/pointer-cursor/link-styling AND no role AND not natively interactive).

cases.why: Every <tr class="listing"> navigates to a detail page via onclick + location.href, with hover highlight, pointer cursor and a visible 'Click a row to open the listing' hint - so the whole row presents as one large link but has no role, no href and no tabindex. The listings are unreachable by keyboard or AT (F42). The table markup itself is correct, and that is all the rubric asked about.
cases.evidence: page L31 (the hint), L45/52/59/66 (<tr class="listing" onclick="openListing('PX-2291')">), L19-21 (cursor:pointer + hover), L77-81 (location.href). Judge summary: 'the heading is properly marked up and the table's column-header associations are valid' - it judged only the facets the rubric enumerates. axe emitted nothing relevant.
cases.fix: Same pseudoControls facet as case-01. A row-level handler is a particularly clean detector signal: a <tr> with an onclick and cursor:pointer whose cells contain no <a>.

cases.why: The flight-search submit control is an with an onclick, cursor:pointer and a hover scale - no role, no tabindex, and an alt ('Round teal search icon with a white magnifying glass') that describes the PICTURE rather than the action, even though the graphic has the word 'Search' baked in. F42/F59: unmistakably a button to a sighted user, nothing to AT. Four obligations existed on this page and all four attached to structurally-correct elements.
cases.evidence: page L40-44 (, no role/tabindex; the inline SVG contains Search). The three field-programmatic-association obligations covered the correctly-labelled From/To/Depart inputs; the fourth was the page-level info-relationships subject. The applicability oracle enumerated no control obligation for the . axe emitted nothing relevant.
cases.fix: Same pseudoControls facet. Note this case ALSO has a live 1.1.1 defect (functional-image alt describing appearance not action) that a 1.1.1 lane should own independently - worth cross-checking against bucket D.

cases.why: A tab strip (Overview / Acquisition / Retention) drawn as underline tabs, with the active tab darker + teal-underlined and switching the panel below. The controls are keyboard-operable (tabindex=0 + Enter/Space) so 2.1.1 passes - the defect is purely relational: each tab is a role-less <div>, the wrapper is not a tablist, the panels are not tabpanels, and the selected state is conveyed by colour alone. The tab/panel relationship and the selected state are visually obvious and programmatically absent.
cases.evidence: page L36-40 (div.tabs with aria-label but NO role; three div.tab with tabindex=0/onclick/onkeydown and no role), L42-62 (three <section class=panel> with no tabpanel role, toggled via `hidden`), L21 (.tab.active colour+underline). info-relationships-v0 has no control/state facet. Cross-check on the plumbing: axe DID emit an `aria-prohibited-attr` INCOMPLETE here (aria-label on the role-less div.tabs) - the one axe signal in this bucket that is hint-eligible (kind==='incomplete') - but orchestrator.js:426 keys hints by exact xpath (`/html/body/div/div[1]`), which can never equal the page-level subject xpath `/page-level::info-relationships` (applicability-oracle.js:167), and llm-adjudicator.js:975 additionally requires `h.sc === subj.sc` (4.1.2 vs 1.3.1). Double-filtered out.
cases.fix: pseudoControls facet + a composite widget-relationship clause (tab/tablist/tabpanel, accordion, listbox). Separately, relax the checkerHint join so a page-level subject inherits element-level hints for its SC (see pattern P7).

cases.why: CSS grid places each label above the OTHER field's input: `.lbl-guests` is (col 1, row 1) but `.in-guests` is (col 2, row 2), while `.in-date` is (col 1, row 2). Verified by screenshot - the box under 'Number of guests' shows placeholder 'MM / DD / YYYY' and is programmatically named 'Preferred date'. A sighted user and a screen-reader user get contradictory label-to-field bindings. The judge cleared all four fields at HIGH confidence on pure source-level for/id matching, ignoring the element-crop and surrounding-region it was handed.
cases.evidence: page L20-28 (.lbl-guests grid-column:1/grid-row:1; .in-guests grid-column:2/grid-row:2; .lbl-date col2/row1; .in-date col1/row2) and L41-51; screenshot at scratchpad/shots/form-label-and-group-relationships-by-context_case-01.png confirms the swap for both pairs (guests/date and mobile/party). field-programmatic-association-v0.md:22-23 states the actual question - 'whether that programmatic name/description fully captures what a sighted user reads' - and L46-47 lists element-crop + surrounding-region as the evidence. The four verdict summaries all say some variant of 'correctly associated with its visible label via a matching for/id pair'. CORPUS METADATA DRIFT: ruleName describes unassociated <span> labels plus title='Field 1'..'Field 5' - none of which is in the shipped page.
cases.fix: Add a fourth failure shape to field-programmatic-association-v0: 'the association points at a DIFFERENT field than the visually adjacent label' - and instruct the judge to verify the for/id target against the crop's geometry, not just the attribute match. A cheap deterministic assist: compare each label's rendered bounding box against its for= target's box and flag when a NEARER field exists.

cases.why: Required status is carried only by red <label> colour plus one prose note ('Fields shown in red are required'). There is no asterisk, no '(required)' token, no required attribute and no aria-required anywhere, so the required relationship is not in any accessible name or description. The rubric's clause 3 covers exactly this shape, and the crops show the red labels, but all six verdicts engaged only clause 1 (for/id) and none mentioned required status at all.
cases.evidence: page L16 (`label.required { color:#c0182b; }`), L27 (the prose note), L32/36/42/52 (class="required" on four labels), and no `required`/`aria-required` anywhere in the file. field-programmatic-association-v0.md:39-44 clause 3: 'a required-field indicator or format hint conveyed ONLY graphically ... that is not reflected anywhere in the accessible name or description - REPRODUCED'. All six rubricVerdicts are LIKELY_OK/high and only assert for/id matching. axe emitted nothing relevant.
cases.fix: Make the three clauses an explicit ordered checklist the judge must answer individually (the verdict schema could require a per-clause disposition), and surface the field's computed `required`/`aria-required` state plus its label's computed colour-vs-siblings as a signal so clause 3 has a deterministic hook. Also cross-check bucket D: this page is simultaneously a 1.4.1 use-of-color failure.

cases.why: Three date-of-birth inputs sit under one visible styled <div> question 'تاريخ الميلاد' with no fieldset/legend and no role=group+aria-labelledby, so the grouping relationship exists only in visual proximity. Each input is named only via title ('سنة'/'شهر'/'يوم' = Year/Month/Day) - generic slot names that are close to the rubric's own 'genuinely ambiguous' exception. The judge over-credited, asserting the title 'matches the visible placeholder and surrounding label context' when nothing programmatically ties the group question to the fields. CONTESTED: Mengqi voted 'no issue' and the rubric's TT 5.C carve-out plausibly permits this.
cases.evidence:
page L40-45 (
تاريخ الميلاد
then three with no fieldset/legend/role=group); screenshot confirms one question over three boxes. field-programmatic-association-v0.md:54-66 - the TT 5.C carve-out ('Do NOT flag a missing group association ... merely because a section heading/question exists nearby') and its exception ('flag it ONLY when the option's own accessible name is GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS without the group question - e.g. options literally named Yes/No/Option A'). Also: axe emitted a DECIDED `label-title-only` violation on all three inputs, but that ruleId is absent from BEST_PRACTICE_RULE_SC (axe-surface.js:62-85) and carries no wcag tag, so surfacedScsFor returns [] and the finding is discarded entirely by the harness.
cases.fix: Widen the exception clause from the literal 'Yes/No/Option A' examples to a stated principle: an accessible name that is a generic SLOT name (Year, Month, Day, Area code, Part 1) rather than a self-describing choice IS ambiguous without the group question. Also add `label-title-only` to axe-surface's best-practice map (review:true, sc 1.3.1). Flag this case for label re-review - it is the most contestable in the bucket.

cases.why: Three of five products are on sale, signalled ONLY by the product name rendering bold + one size larger (.name.promo). No '(Sale)' word, no struck original price, no legend, no colour. A sighted user perceives a distinction that has no programmatic equivalent (WCAG F2). The rubric names 'an emphasis that carries meaning' exactly once in its Judge sentence and then gives it no clause, no signal and no detection guidance.
cases.evidence: page L23-24 (`.name { font-weight:400 } .name.promo { font-weight:700; font-size:1.18rem }`) applied to Harbour Teal / Quartz Rose / Bracken Green; screenshot confirms the three bold+larger names. info-relationships-v0.md:91-93 mentions 'an emphasis that carries meaning' but the 'Common failure patterns' list (L94-172) covers only headings, heading level, table association and lists. llm-adjudicator.js:570-579 shows `s.structure` carries headings/landmarks/tables/lists - no computed font-weight/size/variant outlier facts. Judge summary correctly enumerates the (valid) headings, ul and outline and finds nothing else to look at.
cases.fix: Collect a `styleOutliers[]` signal: text runs whose computed font-weight / font-size / font-variant / font-style differ from their sibling peers within the same repeated component, with no accompanying text or markup difference. Then add an F2 clause. CAVEAT for the paper: with no legend anywhere, even a sighted user cannot decode WHAT the bold means, so a strict 'is information actually conveyed?' reading makes this family contestable - see notes.

cases.why: In-prose references to defined terms (Service, Term, Confidential Information) are distinguished from ordinary words ONLY by font-variant-caps: small-caps, with no <dfn>, no link to the definition and no legend. The defined-term status - a meaningful relationship back to the <dl> in section 1 - is presentation-only (F2). Same missing facet as case-01: no styling-outlier signal and no emphasis clause.
cases.evidence: page L19-20 (`.term { font-variant-caps: small-caps } .ref { font-variant-caps: small-caps }`), L47-48 and L56 (the .ref spans in sections 2 and 3), L30-43 (the <dl> where the terms ARE properly defined). info-relationships-v0.md as above. axe emitted zero findings. The <dl> itself is well-formed, so every facet the rubric CAN see is genuinely clean.
cases.fix: Same styleOutliers signal + F2 clause. Mild severity: legal drafting convention means a sighted reader does decode small-caps as 'defined term', which is what makes it a real (if low-impact) 1.3.1 failure.

cases.why: Each paper's corresponding author is designated only by font-weight:700 on a <span class="corr">, with no '(corresponding author)' text, no asterisk-and-legend and no mailto link - and the intro uses an identical bold (.em-decoy) decoratively, so the marker is ambiguous. Presentation-only relationship (F2), same uncovered facet.
cases.evidence: page L20-21 (`.corr { font-weight:700 } .em-decoy { font-weight:700 }`), L39/48/56/65 (the .corr spans), L32-33 (the decoy). info-relationships-v0.md as above. axe emitted only color-contrast and page-has-heading-one (advisory).
cases.fix: Same styleOutliers signal + F2 clause. The decoy is a deliberate precision trap: any detector must not fire on a single decorative bold run, only on a bold run that recurs in the SAME structural slot across repeated components (here, one author name per article).

cases.why: The 'Verified seller' badge SVG (aria-hidden, inside span[role=presentation], no author name) measures 22x22px. decorativeSuspect() requires minDim >= 24 (V3_DECORATIVE_MIN_DIM), so the badge mints NO 1.1.1 obligation at all; the page's single 1.1.1 obligation landed on a healthy sibling (div.product-photo[role=img] with a good aria-label) and the judge correctly cleared THAT element. The verdict is on the wrong element, but the cause is upstream: the defective element is invisible to the oracle by construction.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer probe: badge svg box = 22x22, svgLiveText=false, parent textContent=''. applicability-oracle.js:151 `const squareGate = Math.max(1, Number(process.env.V3_DECORATIVE_MIN_DIM) || 24)`; :158 elongated escape needs aspect >= 4 (aspect here = 1). applicability-oracle.js:284 skips removedFromA11yTree images; :291 decorativeConflict needs an author name (none here). Page footer states the badge is the sole verification signal; unverified sellers render without it.
cases.fix: Add a badge/status-icon lane to decorativeSuspect(): a removed-from-tree image below the 24px square gate is still a suspect when it sits inside a small labelled row/flex container alongside text (an icon whose PRESENCE-vs-ABSENCE is the datum). Alternatively drop the square gate to ~16 for images inside [class*=badge]/[class*=status]/inline flex rows only, so ordinary 8px spacers stay excluded.

cases.why: A 640x280 <canvas role='presentation'> draws a complete tariff-comparison table (peak/off-peak unit price, standing charge, avg annual bill for 3 tariffs) and the page contains NO HTML table, dl, or text duplicate of those numbers. decorative-image-verification-v0 fired on the correct element and cleared it by asserting the data is 'redundantly present in a real HTML table visible in the surrounding region' — that table does not exist. The judge almost certainly read the canvas's OWN rendered pixels in the surrounding-region screenshot as a real HTML table.
cases.evidence: Page source case-02.html:37 (canvas role=presentation) + :79-97 (the four data rows drawn into it); the only other content is a <select> of tariff names. Puppeteer probe: canvas parent .chart-wrap textContent = '' ⇒ nearbyText is UNDEFINED. decorative-image-verification-v0.md:58-59 says 'if the surrounding text is absent and the image is ambiguous, return PARTIAL' — the judge returned NOT REPRODUCED instead.
cases.fix: Harden the rubric's redundancy clause: when `decorativeMarking.nearbyText` is null/empty, PARTIAL is mandatory, not advisory — a data-bearing crop with zero nearbyText can never be 'redundant'. Also forbid crediting redundancy against content the judge can only see INSIDE the element crop.

cases.why: The safety-critical dosing SVG is aria-hidden, so its <text> nodes are removed from the a11y tree along with everything else. The harness handed the judge two signals that both say the opposite: (1) `nearbyText` is computed as textOf(el.parentElement), and for an inline SVG the parent's innerText INCLUDES the SVG's own hidden <text> — so the redundancy test is self-satisfying; (2) `svgLiveText:true` ships an uncertainReason literally stating 'its text is REAL and machine-readable'. The judge's summary quotes both: 'fully conveyed by the live text within the SVG itself and reproduced in the nearbyText'.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer probe on case-04.html: nearbyText = 'Morning 2 tablets Midday 1 tablet Night 1 tablet TAKE WITH FOOD DO NOT crush — swallow whole | Take your morning and midday doses as shown above...' — i.e. the SVG's own suppressed text. act-page-collect.js:607-613 (`if (el.parentElement) bits.push(textOf(el.parentElement))`, textOf = innerText||textContent, :145). llm-adjudicator.js:350-351 emits svgLiveText with no removedFromA11yTree guard. Page caption (case-04.html:83) restates none of the regimen.
cases.fix: Two one-line fixes. (a) act-page-collect.js:610 — subtract the element's own subtree before taking parent text (clone the parent, remove the element, then textOf), so nearbyText means text OUTSIDE the image. (b) llm-adjudicator.js:350 — gate the svgLiveText steer on `element.removedFromA11yTree !== true`, and when the SVG IS removed from the tree emit the inverse steer: 'this SVG renders live <text> but the whole subtree is aria-hidden, so NONE of it reaches AT'.

cases.why: Four of five elements in the image map carry alt text describing the region's APPEARANCE ('Large blue rectangle in the top-left corner') instead of the link destination — a real 1.1.1/H24 failure for functional non-text content. The collector never sees any : they have zero-size client rects and the enumeration loop skips anything failing visible(), which requires width>0 && height>0. The only obligation minted was on the parent , whose own alt is fine, so the judge cleared correctly on the element it was given.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer probe: `map area` getBoundingClientRect() = {w:0,h:0} (parent img = 600x360). act-page-collect.js:139-144 `visible()` returns false for zero-size; :451-454 `if (!_subset) { if (!visible(el)) continue; }`. Page case-03.html:37-46 shows 4 appearance-alt areas + 1 correct control area.
cases.fix: Special-case <area> in the collector's visibility filter: use the area's `coords` (or the owning img's box) as its geometry rather than its own empty client rect, so each <area> is enumerated as a link-role image element and mints its own non-text-content + link-purpose obligation.

cases.why: The print button's ONLY accessible name is img alt='inkjet printer' (its visible 'Print' caption is aria-hidden), so the control is announced by the depicted device rather than its action — the exact 'functional image whose name must convey the ACTION' failure. alt-text-adequacy-v0 has that clause, the judge correctly identified that the img IS the control's sole name, and then cleared it anyway ('so inkjet printer adequately identifies the control's action (printing)'). The rubric covers this; the judge was too lenient.
cases.evidence: Page case-04.html:55-59 (button onclick=window.print(), img alt='inkjet printer', span.cap aria-hidden='true'>Print). alt-text-adequacy-v0.md:50-58 (the 'Wrong purpose for a functional image — ONLY when the image IS the control's SOLE name' clause). The two sibling buttons in the same bar are named for their action ('Add to Apple Wallet', 'Email boarding pass'), which is the intended in-page contrast.
cases.fix: Tighten the clause with a positive test rather than only the negative carve-out: when the image IS the sole name, require the name to contain an ACTION/destination (a verb or a target), and state that a bare noun naming the depicted object ('printer', 'envelope', 'magnifier', 'floppy disk') is insufficient. The current clause spends 8 lines telling the judge NOT to flag and 1 line telling it when to flag.

cases.why: The metro map's aria-describedby target lists the four lines and their termini but states no interchange, so a screen-reader user cannot plan a trip requiring a change — the map's whole purpose. long-description-completeness-v0 fired on the right element and returned UNCERTAIN with the verbatim reason 'Cannot determine if aria-describedby target conveys equivalent information without inspecting the referenced element's content'. The resolved long-description TEXT is never put in the signal bundle: nearbyText is surfaced only inside `s.decorativeMarking`, which is built only for removed-from-tree images.

Page case-04.html:30-32 (img aria-describedby=metroDesc) vs :35-43 (the description, no interchange named).
cases.fix: Add a `longDescription` signal to buildSignals for any element with complexImageHint: resolve aria-describedby ids, the enclosing figcaption, and any <details>/adjacent data table to TEXT, and hand it to the rubric with an explicit 'compare this text to the pixels' steer. This is the same nearbyText plumbing, just un-gated from the decorative branch.

cases.why: The loan-decision flowchart's figcaption enumerates all six boxes but states none of the Yes/No branch conditions, so the reader learns the vocabulary and not the logic (F67). long-description-completeness-v0 fired on the right element and abstained: 'Could not verify whether the SVG flowchart's text alternative conveys equivalent information without querying the accessibility node' — the same missing-text-alternative signal as case-04. Notably the page contains a prose <aside> that literally spells out the defect, and the judge still could not commit.
cases.evidence: Same code path as case-04: llm-adjudicator.js:403 (nearbyText gated to the decorativeMarking/removed-from-tree branch only), so an IN-tree figure image gets crops but no caption text. Page case-03.html:72-77 (figcaption lists boxes only) vs :59-69 (the Yes/No edges that carry the logic). The rubric gate is llm-adjudicator.js:169.
cases.fix: Same as case-04 (resolve + hand over the long-description text). Secondarily: `query_ax_node` IS a registered tool (cdp-tool-catalog.js:16) — if the judge names it as the blocker, the orchestrator should force-invoke it rather than accept an UNCERTAIN.

cases.why: The org chart's figcaption is a flat roster of seven name/title pairs and contains no reporting relationship at all; the hierarchy exists only in the connecting <path> lines. The judge cleared at high confidence asserting the caption 'conveys all personnel, roles, and reporting relationships'. Unlike its two siblings it did not abstain — it asserted a property of the caption that the caption plainly lacks.
cases.evidence: Page case-07.html:73-79 (figcaption: 'The department comprises seven people: ...' — a comma list, zero 'reports to') vs :35-42 (the six <path> edges encoding the hierarchy). Contrast with cases 03/04 in the same rule family, which returned UNCERTAIN on the same evidence shape.
cases.fix: Add a structure checklist to long-description-completeness-v0 for relational images: for a chart/diagram/map, require the judge to name the RELATION type the image encodes (edges/branches/interchanges/hierarchy) and then verify that relation appears in the text — a roster of the nodes must be judged INSUFFICIENT by construction.

cases.why: The hero h1 and role line are built from Mathematical Sans-Serif Bold/Italic codepoints (U+1D5E6 etc.) that render as 'Sumi Tanaka / Designer & Illustrator' but are not letters to AT, with no plain-Latin equivalent. No obligation was minted for either element: the collector's hasGlyphText predicate only covers Private Use Area codepoints and a Cyrillic/Greek + Latin MIX, and Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols (U+1D400-1D7FF) are in neither range. The one 1.1.1 obligation on the page landed on the decorative gradient .avatar div[role=img], which is genuinely fine.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer probe: h1 hasGlyphText=false, role p hasGlyphText=false (both computed with the collector's exact expression). act-page-collect.js:621 `[...ownTxt].some(c in 0xE000-0xF8FF | 0xF0000-0xFFFFD | 0x100000-0x10FFFD) || (/[Ѐ-ӿͰ-Ͽ]/.test(t) && /[a-zA-Z]/.test(t))`; applicability-oracle.js:316 gates glyph-text-alternative on it. Meanwhile `detectConfusableText` DOES handle this: node run returns {hasConfusables:true, kinds:['math-styled'], asciiFold:'Sumi Tanaka'} — but confusable-text is only a SIGNAL added in llm-adjudicator.js:236 for elements that ALREADY have an obligation, never an applicability gate.

One-line change that turns an existing, tested detector into the applicability gate it was built for. Note there is also no glyph-text-alternative-v0.md rubric file — the family (applicability-oracle.js:79, catalog.js:178) routes to name-role-state; confirm which rubric would judge it.

cases.why: The headline sale price renders '$300' from Cyrillic З + О + О with no aria-label, so AT announces gibberish. Two independent gates miss it: (1) the collector's hasGlyphText requires a Latin letter in the SAME text to flag a Cyrillic run, and '$ЗОО' has none; (2) even confusable-text.js's homoglyph-full lane would not fire — it requires >= 4 letters and this word has 3. The single obligation landed on the .photo div[role=img], which has a fine aria-label. Marginality note: the true price also appears as plain '$300' in the Add-to-cart button, which partially mitigates the barrier.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer probe: span.now ownTxt='$ЗОО', hasGlyphText=false. node: detectConfusableText('$ЗОО','en') -> {hasConfusables:false} (confusable-text.js:94 `letters.length >= 4`). Page case-05.html:39 vs :50 (button 'Add to cart — $300'). CORPUS HYGIENE: case-05.html:36 leaks the answer in prose ('genuinely encoded (Latin O U+004F + digit 0 U+0030)').

cases.why: The theme gives .course a and .course strong byte-identical presentation (color rgb(157,27,61), weight 700, text-decoration none), so 'maroon + bold' is not a link-specific cue — half the maroon-bold phrases are links and half are emphasis, and only the href separates them. use-of-color-v0's F73 clause says ANY of underline/weight/italic/lightness satisfies, so the judge's 'distinguished from surrounding body text by bold weight' clears legitimately per the rubric as written. The rubric has no clause for a cue SHARED with non-link content. Aggravator: one verdict (p[5]/a[1] 'office-hours sign-up') claims 'a visible underline' that does not exist.

This is the same 'compare against the siblings' framing the already-written `use-of-color-adequacy` micro-check uses (micro-checks.js:132-142) but the free-form rubric lacks.

cases.why: The defect lives entirely in the post-submit error summary: three of eight <li> rows are re-colored #cf1d1d and the other five stay #67707a, with no 'Error:' word, icon, or count — hue is the only marker of which fields failed, and the inputs below carry plain borders. All 8 use-of-color obligations were minted on form controls; ZERO were minted on any <li>. The oracle attaches use-of-color ONLY to links and form fields, so the actual color-only surface was never asked about.

Page case-03.html:22-23 (`.errsum li { color:#67707a } .errsum li.bad { color:#cf1d1d }`) and :49-58 (the eight rows, three .bad). That single fact catches error-summary rows, legend swatches, status rows and category-colored links, and is bounded (only fires where a peer set exists).

cases.why: The confirm-password field's live mismatch is signalled only by a red ring (box-shadow + border #d31f2f) toggled by JS. The judge targeted exactly the right element and cleared it because 'the red border is accompanied by the visible hint text Must match the new password above' — but that hint is a PERMANENT instruction rendered identically in the matched state (its sibling 'New password' field carries the same kind of static hint), so it carries no state information. use-of-color-v0 says 'the same state ALSO carrying text/an icon/a shape is NOT a barrier' without ever distinguishing a state-dependent cue from a static instruction.
cases.evidence:
Page case-04.html:22-23 (`input.mismatch { box-shadow:0 0 0 2px #d31f2f; border-color:#d31f2f }`), :51 (`

Must match the new password above.

` — static markup, never touched by the script), :60-67 (sync() toggles only the class). Compare :45, an identical static .hint on the non-error field.
cases.fix: Add to use-of-color-v0's F81 section: the non-color cue must be STATE-DEPENDENT — it must appear/change when the state does. A permanently-rendered instruction, placeholder, or format hint that reads the same in the pass state does not satisfy 1.4.1. Practical test for the judge: 'would this text also be present if the field were valid?' If yes, it is not a cue.

cases.why: The failed password field gets a 2px #d92020 border while the valid email field keeps a 2px #8a8f94 border; the banner is generic and never names the field, so hue is the only per-field signal. The obligation landed on the right element and the judge abstained with 'Could not confirm whether red-border invalid state has non-color cue without grayscale render'. The tool exists (`render_with_overrides` with transform=grayscale/protanopia/…, CDP Emulation.setEmulatedVisionDeficiency) and is explicitly DECLARED as required evidence for SC 1.4.1 — but nothing enforces that declaration, so the judge never got the render.

Grep for requiredToolFor/REQUIRED_TOOL_ROUTING across scripts/ finds NO consumer — the only force-invoke in the pipeline is the hard-coded 2.4.4 resolve_destination at orchestrator.js:357. Tool is registered: cdp-tool-catalog.js:43-44, cdp-tools.js:801-828/1468. Page case-01.html:30-31, :52, :58.

Independently, sharpen the rubric: use-of-color-v0.md:61-64 already says the grayscale/lightness escape is F73-ONLY and must NOT be applied to F81 red=invalid states — so the judge should have returned REPRODUCED here without any render. Add an explicit 'do not abstain pending a grayscale render on an F81 state' line.

cases.why: Identical failure to case-01. The 'Number of children' field is flagged by aria-invalid='true' driving a red border, with no visible error text, icon or '(error)' marker, and a generic banner. The judge targeted the right element and abstained with 'Could not confirm whether red border survives grayscale without rendering the element'. Also note aria-invalid is a programmatic exposure and does NOT satisfy 1.4.1, which is about the sighted color-blind user.

cases.why: The donation pie has five unlabelled <path> wedges; the wedge->program binding lives only in a color-swatch legend whose swatches are aria-hidden, and the caption's one pointer is 'the largest wedge, shown in teal' — which itself requires perceiving teal. The page's single 1.4.1 obligation was minted on the 'Give monthly' anchor at the bottom of the card. The SVG and the legend <li>s can never mint a use-of-color obligation because the gate is links + form fields only.
cases.evidence: applicability-oracle.js:313. Page case-02.html:41-48 (five unlabelled wedges), :50-56 (legend, `<span class='sw' aria-hidden='true'>` swatches), :59-65 (caption naming amounts but binding only 'teal'), :68 (the donate <a> that got the obligation). The SVG does get a 1.4.11 non-text-contrast obligation (applicability-oracle.js:264) — wrong SC, so it cannot score for the 1.4.1 label.

Cheap, high-precision predicate — a legend is a very distinctive markup shape and it is exactly where the 'which color means what' obligation belongs.

cases.why: Three metro routes are drawn as polylines that differ only by stroke color, every station is an identical white dot, and the legend keys each route name to a solid color swatch with no pattern, dash, shape or in-line label. Route identity is conveyed by hue alone. The page's single 1.4.1 obligation was minted on the unrelated 'Which line are you taking?' <select> in the trip planner.

Two compounding failures: the <tr> can never mint a use-of-color obligation (gate is links + form fields), and the saved state does not exist in the at-rest DOM, so even a correctly-targeted obligation would have to drive the button first. The four obligations landed on the date inputs.

cases.why: Links that open a new browser tab are teal (#1c8a86) and same-window links are blue (#14467a); nothing else differs — no '(opens in new window)' text, no external-link icon — and the only explanation is a colour-keyed prose legend ('Links shown in teal open in a new browser tab'), which itself requires perceiving teal. The obligations DID land on all ten correct <a> elements, but every verdict answers the F73 link-vs-prose question ('the link is underlined, so not colour alone') — the underline observation is factually right and completely beside the point. use-of-color-v0's taxonomy is link-vs-prose (F73) and widget state (F81); it has no clause for two PEER elements distinguished from EACH OTHER by hue.
cases.evidence: Puppeteer computed styles: ul.docs a.local = rgb(20,70,122) underline; a.newwin = rgb(28,138,134) underline — identical weight/decoration, hue-only difference. Page case-02.html:17-18 (`a.local{color:#14467a} a.newwin{color:#1c8a86}`), :31-32 (the colour-keyed legend), :38/:44/:46/:52 (target=_blank only on .newwin). use-of-color-v0.md:19-31 (only F73 and F81 are enumerated).
cases.fix: Add a third failure mode to use-of-color-v0: CATEGORY/GROUPING BY HUE — when peer elements of the same role are split into classes by colour alone (link destination type, row category, map route, legend key, tag/label group), the category membership is conveyed by colour alone regardless of whether each element is individually distinguishable from prose. Pair it with the collector's peer-colour-differential fact so the judge is TOLD which peers differ.

cases.why: The page is a STATIC post-submit error state (no <script>): input#phone value="12025550143" is all digits, aria-invalid="true", aria-describedby-> #error-phone which reads 'Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number'. cases.why: The three .inline-ref links are styled IDENTICALLY to the surrounding prose (color:#202124 = body color, text-decoration:none, weight 400). Colour is therefore not used to distinguish them AT ALL, so F73's precondition ('links distinguished from surrounding text only by colour') is not met and SC 1.4.1 is not engaged — the corpus label `inapplicable` is right. The rubric has no applicability precondition; its only escape is a >=3:1 link-vs-prose LIGHTNESS separation, which makes 1:1 (no colour difference whatsoever) the maximally-failing value. The SC is thus inverted: less colour difference produces more barrier.
cases.evidence: Judge summary literally reads 'shares the exact same color (rgba(32,33,36), 1:1 contrast ratio' -> LIKELY_BARRIER. Rubric clause: scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/use-of-color-v0.md:22-27 and the carve-out at :56-60. Page CSS: eval/act-augmented/1.4.1/pages/inline-links-color-only-no-other-cue/case-07.html:20 `.legal .inline-ref { color:#202124; text-decoration:none; font-weight:400 }` against body color #202124 (line 8). axe link-in-text-block PASSES all 4 links on this page (verified live). Two of the three barrier summaries also cite colours that do not exist on the page (#2563eb/#374151, #555555) — fabricated measurements.
cases.fix: use-of-color-v0.md — add an APPLICABILITY PRECONDITION before the F73 bullet: if the link's computed colour is the same as (or within ~1.1:1 of) the enclosing prose colour and no other styling differs, colour is NOT the distinguishing means, F73 does not apply, return NOT REPRODUCED (optionally note it as a different-SC concern). Never let a 1:1 ratio read as a colour-alone failure.

cases.why: 2.4.3 requires focus order to preserve MEANING AND OPERABILITY, not to match visual order. Here two INDEPENDENT regions — a course-content column and a site-wide donation aside explicitly labelled 'This appears site-wide and is unrelated to your coursework' — are ordered aside-first in the DOM and painted left-first by flex `order`. Order WITHIN each region is preserved, no tabindex is used, no task is impaired: a keyboard user tabs the donation form, then the whole course column in its logical order. The rubric explicitly forbids exactly this reasoning; the judge did it anyway, resting the verdict solely on 'inverting the logical left-to-right reading order visible on screen' and never identifying an impaired task.

Rubric guards violated: focus-order-meaning-v0.md:23-25 ('NOT a barrier: a focus order that follows the logical/visible flow ... even if it is not strictly top-to-bottom') and :43-45 ('2.4.3 is about preserving MEANING/operability, not matching DOM source order or strict visual top-to-bottom'). Page: eval/act-augmented/2.4.3/pages/css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning/case-03.html:17-20, 46-54.

Add a worked non-barrier example: two independent regions reordered by CSS flex `order` with no tabindex.

cases.why: The harness is RIGHT and the label is wrong. The tooltip is positioned `top:135%`, leaving an 11px dead gap between the sync chip and the popup. mouseleave fires on the chip the instant the pointer enters that gap, the popup goes visibility:hidden, and because a hidden element cannot receive mouseenter the popup can NEVER be reached by pointer. That is a direct failure of the Hoverable condition ('the pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing'). The scenario metadata asserts it 'meets all three conditions' and is 'Verified' — it is not.
cases.evidence: Direct pointer-travel probe (scratchpad/hover-travel.js): trigger box bottom y=46.39, tooltip top y=57.42 => verticalGapPx=11.03. Sampling a straight-line travel from trigger centre to tooltip centre every 2px: shown=true through y=43.9, shown=false from (1168.7, 47.1) onward, endShown=FALSE — the tooltip never comes back. Persistent (dwell) and Escape-dismiss both PASS; only Hoverable fails. Page: eval/act-augmented/1.4.13/pages/persistent-auto-timeout-vs-valid-info-invalidation/case-05.html:24-29 (.detail top:135%) and :81-86 (chip mouseleave -> hide).
cases.fix: Corpus fix: flip `expected` to failed for this case, or repair the page (top:100%, or add a transparent bridge / padding so the trigger box abuts the popup). No harness change — the hover-content-v0 verdict text ('it disappears when the pointer moves from the trigger down onto the tooltip content itself') is factually accurate.

cases.why: The harness is RIGHT and the label is wrong. The page's Escape handler is self-defeating: `close(); term.focus();` — and `term` has a `focus` listener bound to `open`, so on the POINTER-HOVER path Escape closes the tooltip and instantly re-opens it, while also yanking keyboard focus onto the trigger. SC 1.4.13 Dismissible requires a mechanism to dismiss 'without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus'; here Escape neither dismisses nor leaves focus alone. The tooltip is position:absolute over the following paragraph, so it obscures content and the Dismissible exemption does not apply. Hoverable and Persistent genuinely pass — Dismissible is the failing condition, and the deterministic tri-probe's anyPropertyFails is correct.

KEYBOARD path — after Tab {open:'true'}; after Escape {open:'false', display:'none'} (works only because focus was already on the term, making term.focus() a no-op). Pointer-travel probe separately shows verticalGapPx = -5.25 (tooltip OVERLAPS the trigger) and everHidden=false, so Hoverable is fine. Page: eval/act-augmented/1.4.13/pages/hover-content-no-keyboard-focus-trigger-path/case-06.html:95-110. cases.fix: Corpus fix: flip `expected` to failed, or repair the page (do not call term.focus() when the tooltip was hover-triggered, or guard the focus listener with a flag). The scenario text claims 'dismissible with Escape without moving focus' — precisely what the shipped page fails to do; classic metadata-vs-shipped drift.

cases.why: CONTESTED, leaning harness-correct. The invalid amount field is distinguished from valid fields ONLY by border colour (#7c0c12 vs #c1c7cd) — no icon, no per-field text, no aria-invalid. The corpus's stated justification is that the two border colours differ by 6.42:1 in luminance so the distinction survives greyscale. But that lightness escape is an F73/G183 construct scoped to LINKS distinguished from surrounding TEXT; F81 ('identifying required or error fields using color differences only') offers no such escape, and G183 additionally requires a second cue on hover/focus, which is absent here. The only non-colour cue is a generic role=alert banner ('review the data and try again') that never names the field. The rubric's CRITICAL GUARD takes exactly this position deliberately.

F81 title per wcag-techniques/techniques-manifest.json: 'Failure of SC 1.4.1 due to identifying required or error fields using color differences only' — listed `failure`, with no lightness carve-out. Page: eval/act-augmented/1.4.1/pages/error-validation-color-only/case-07.html:27-28, 46, 56.

Escalate as a label/interpretation dispute: both annotators voted no-issue, so it needs an adjudicator ruling on whether lightness separation satisfies F81.

cases.why: CONTESTED, leaning harness-correct. The corpus label rests explicitly on H80 ('H80 Example 2 done correctly') — but W3C classifies H80 as an ADVISORY technique for 2.4.4, not a sufficient one, precisely because a preceding heading is not reliably surfaced with the link. WCAG's programmatically-determined-link-context definition enumerates same sentence / paragraph / list item / table cell (+ its header) and does not include a preceding heading. Each link's actual enclosing block text is 'Download:', and the nine names are format-only tokens ('HTML', 'PDF (3.2 MB)', 'RTF (1.1 MB)') repeated identically across three documents. The harness's collector deliberately restricts 2.4.4 context to the ANCESTOR chain (a documented round-3 FN fix), so this outcome is by design, not by accident.
