patterns.name: focusRisk only sees INLINE focus attributes, never addEventListener
patterns.description: applicability-oracle.js:268 gates no-keyboard-trap on `focusable && (inModal || focusRisk)`. focusRisk (act-page-collect.js:577-580) is true only when the element carries an INLINE onblur/onfocus/onfocusout ATTRIBUTE, or sits inside a dialog/menu/listbox/grid/tablist or a modal|overlay|dialog|popup|lightbox class. Measured across all 20 2.1.2 pages in this bucket: ZERO inline focus handlers anywhere; every trap is wired with addEventListener('keydown'|'blur'|'focus'). Ten of these pages have the trap on plainly visible, collected, non-modal controls whose containers are role=group / a bare <table> / nothing — so both disjuncts fail and the family never mints. The predicate cannot detect the self-refocus trap it was explicitly written for (input-gate case-02 is the proof: addEventListener('blur') doing exactly what hasAttribute('onblur') looks for).
patterns.proposedFix: Add a listener-derived disjunct to focusRisk. The collector already captures registered listener types per element (`listenerTypes`, consumed by the 2.1.1 keyboard-orphan detector at build-v3.js:820-826), so: focusRisk ||= (self or ancestor has a registered 'keydown' | 'blur' | 'focusout' listener). This is a fact the collector already has and does not widen enumeration to bare focusables.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 10 cases in this bucket; likely most of the 29/38 zero-obligation 2.1.2 cases in the full run

patterns.name: Collect is resting-DOM only — a closed modal/menu/grid is a structural blind spot
patterns.description: act-page-collect.js:452-453 drops every element that is not visible in the resting DOM, so the contents of a display:none modal or an unopened menu/calendar are never collected. Both 2.1.2 gates then starve: no-keyboard-trap has no focusable subject and composite-arrow-trap (oracle:320) has no role=menu/role=grid container. The intended escape hatch, dynamic-subjects.js, is a dead end here: it only expands subjects that an EXPERIMENT reported, and no experiment runs because no static obligation was minted — a chicken-and-egg. Confirmed per case by listing the exact invisible-at-load focusables and then re-probing after clicking the opener (all five are genuine traps that Escape does not release).
patterns.proposedFix: A reveal-and-recollect pass before enumeration: activate openers (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded=false, aria-controls, [role=button]/button whose click reveals a role=dialog/menu/listbox/grid) and feed the newly-visible subjects through dynamic-subjects.js's existing fingerprinted discovery path. reveal-state-runner.js / reveal-checklist.js already have most of this machinery for the hover-content family.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 5 cases in this bucket; generalises to every dialog/menu-shaped page in the corpus

patterns.name: Empty or hidden live regions are dropped before the liveRegion fact is read
patterns.description: This is the half of the 4.1.3 story the coordinator's lead did not have, and it refutes the assumption that a case with a valid pre-existing live region is safe. All five of these pages DO carry a textbook-correct role=status + aria-live=polite region in the resting DOM. They mint nothing anyway, because a status container at rest is either EMPTY (zero width/height) or visually hidden (opacity:0 / display:none until shown), and the collector's main-walk visibility filter at act-page-collect.js:452-453 runs BEFORE the liveRegion fact at :627. The fact's own comment — 'Kept even when empty (a live region is typically populated dynamically, so it has no text at collect time)' — describes an intent the code never reaches. Corollary for the cross-bucket asymmetry: a page whose live region happens to be non-empty or has a min-height at rest (e.g. removal-of-status case-06, .avail{min-height:22px}) DOES mint and lands in missedAgree; an otherwise identical page whose region is empty lands in noObligation. The outcome label is decided by resting CSS, not by the defect.
patterns.proposedFix: Exempt live-region candidates from the visibility filter: `if (!visible(el) && !(aria-live in {polite,assertive,off} || implicit live role)) continue;`. One line, and it makes the collector match its own documented contract.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 5 cases in this bucket; plus it removes the empty-vs-nonempty coin flip that splits identical defects across the noObligation and missedAgree buckets

patterns.name: 4.1.3 keys on the live region, so the canonical no-live-region defect is unreachable
patterns.description: CONFIRMED as the coordinator described, with the exact condition: applicability-oracle.js:241 `if (el.liveRegion === true) fams.push('status-message')`, where liveRegion is computed at act-page-collect.js:627 as `aria-live in {polite,assertive}` OR `role in {status,alert,log,progressbar,marquee,timer}`, on the resting DOM. A status message that is born with its region (innerHTML string, createElement-then-append, setAttribute-at-fill-time, template clone, custom-element connectedCallback), or that has no live markup at all, can never satisfy the gate — the element needing the obligation is by definition not a live region. aria-live='off' (wrong-live-region case-01) fails for the same reason and is arguably the worst case, since 'off' is a stronger smell than no attribute at all.
patterns.proposedFix: Mint 4.1.3 from the ACTION side as well as the region side: a non-navigating activation control (or a page-level settle-window MutationObserver, for the timer-driven case-04) owes 'was the resulting status announced'. Treat aria-live='off' as a live-region suspect with a politenessOff fact.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 7 cases in this bucket; combined with the empty-region pattern above this accounts for 13 of the bucket's 15 4.1.3 cases

patterns.name: status-detector's trigger set excludes every typeless <button>
patterns.description: status-detector.js:53 computes `const type = (el.getAttribute('type') || el.type || '').toLowerCase()` and then excludes `type === 'submit'`. HTMLButtonElement.type defaults to 'submit', so EVERY <button> without an explicit type attribute is excluded — in or out of a form. The very next line, `if (el.tagName === 'BUTTON' && !type && el.form) return false;`, is unreachable dead code and documents that the intended exclusion was only the default-submit-inside-a-form case. Measured on announced-text case-03: 8 bare <button onclick=...> controls, none in a form, triggersTotal = 0.
patterns.proposedFix: Use only `el.getAttribute('type')` for the submit/reset/image test and keep the existing in-form default-submit rule (which then becomes live). One line.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here directly, but it re-arms the 4.1.3 instrument on the most common button-authoring pattern across the whole corpus

patterns.name: 4.1.3 instrument findings are routed to a non-ledger triage queue and never scored
patterns.description:
build-v3.js:855-869 puts 4.1.3 in TRIAGE_SCS, so status-detector findings become `triageCandidates` — explicitly 'review packets, NOT PROVISIONAL ledger rows ... they never clear/barrier'. On is-it-a-status case-05 the detector produced six correct findings naming the exact defective

, and the case still scored noObligation. This is a correct detection discarded by design, not a detection failure. 4.1.3 is the only SC in TRIAGE_SCS that has both a working instrument and a shipped rubric (status-message-v0).
patterns.proposedFix: Mint an obligation from a 4.1.3 status-detector finding on the finding's xpath, exactly as build-v3.js:412-435 already does for checker-uncertainty findings, landing auto-PARTIAL for an LLM PROVISIONAL fill. Remove 4.1.3 from TRIAGE_SCS.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case in this bucket; more once the trigger-set bug above is fixed, since the detector currently reaches almost no pages

patterns.name: Build aborts on any disabled control with text, and the scorer records it as noObligation
patterns.description: CROSS-CUTTING — affects every SC, not just this bucket, and I found it by accident. coverage-registry.js:37 requires the text-contrast family for any element with text (`when: (el) => factHasText(el)`), but applicability-oracle.js:223 withholds it when `el.inactiveText === true` (the deliberate 1.4.3 inactive-UI-component exemption added to stop vision contrast FPs on greyed controls). The two disagree, the fail-closed Rule-16 coverage check fires, build-v3 returns `{ok:false, results:null}`, and scoreCase (fp-experiments/score-lib.js:22) turns a null ledger into zero obligations — indistinguishable in the record from a genuine applicability miss. Reproduced end to end on removal-of-status case-06: built.ok=false, the coverage-gap error names the disabled 'Reserve this table' button, ledger empty, yet the standalone oracle mints the correct 4.1.3 obligation on the same collect. Blast radius estimate over the run: 7 of the 82 noObligation rows (9%) contain a disabled/aria-disabled control versus 2 of the other 323 rows (1%) — roughly a 10x enrichment.
patterns.proposedFix: (1) Mirror the exemption in the registry: `{ id: 'has-text', when: (el) => factHasText(el) && el.inactiveText !== true, families: ['text-contrast'] }`. (2) Independently, make a failed build a distinct scored outcome ('buildError') rather than silently collapsing to noObligation — otherwise harness crashes are permanently miscounted as applicability gaps in every future analysis of this corpus.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases in this bucket (1 decisively); ~7 across the run, and it unblocks any other fix on those pages

patterns.name: Sub-documents and shadow trees carry hard-coded trap-free facts or are not collected at all
patterns.description: Three distinct sub-document holes, all producing the same zero-obligation result and all confirmed by probing focus across the boundary. (a) SAME-ORIGIN IFRAME: the in-frame collection branch literally writes `inModal: false, focusRisk: false` on every record (act-page-collect.js:873), so oracle:268's second conjunct is unsatisfiable for any in-frame focusable — the two cross-format iframe cases and the modal srcdoc case. (b) SHADOW DOM: walkShadow (act-page-collect.js:896-918) collects ONLY <iframe>/<frame> nodes found inside shadow roots, so a component whose entire UI lives in an open shadow root contributes nothing. (c) <object>/<embed>: the sub-document traversal selector is 'iframe, frame' only (act-page-collect.js:824), so an SVG document loaded via <object> is never descended.
patterns.proposedFix: (a) Compute inModal/focusRisk in the in-frame branch the same way as the top-document loop — they are plain DOM reads and are frame-agnostic. (b) Collect focusable/text-bearing shadow-root elements, not only shadow iframes, reusing the existing '>>shadow' xpath namespacing. (c) Add `object[data], embed` to the traversal selector. Additionally, a frame-boundary trap signal (any same-origin sub-document whose focusables form a closed Tab cycle) would cover all three shapes at once.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 5 cases in this bucket

patterns.name: 1.4.1 use-of-color only ever attaches to links and form fields
patterns.description:
applicability-oracle.js:313 (mirrored in coverage-registry.js:70) gates the use-of-color family on `role === 'link' || isFormField || FORMFIELD_ROLE`. FORMFIELD_ROLE excludes button/switch/checkbox, and isFormField (act-page-collect.js:153) is input/select/textarea only. So SC 1.4.1 is structurally invisible on charts (,
), on colour-coded controls (
patterns.proposedFix: Three layers. (1) Widen the surface in oracle:313 + registry:70 to `|| el.isImage === true || IMG_ROLE.test(role) || WIDGET_ROLE.test(role)` — recovers the 5 chart/control cases. (2) Add a legend-keyed-colour nominator to the collector: an element whose ONLY computed-style difference from its same-tag siblings is colour/background-colour, on a page whose text contains a colour-mapping phrase ('shown in green', 'red = ...') or a swatch legend — recovers the remaining 4 (td/article/span) cases. (3) Add G14/F13/F81-control clauses to use-of-color-v0.md, and tighten the existing F73 clause so an equal-colour link is judged inapplicable rather than a barrier (kills the FPs). Route all of these to the already-wired render_with_overrides grayscale tool (required-tool-routing.js:10) so the second-cue question is answered deterministically rather than by eyeballing a crop.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 10 of 11 in this bucket; run-wide 1.4.1 has 11 failed/noObligation + 10 failed/missedAgree, and the FP fix touches the 5 1.4.1 false positives

patterns.name: coverage-registry <-> oracle drift on inactiveText aborts the ENTIRE build
patterns.description: The 1.4.3 'inactive UI component' exemption was added to the oracle (applicability-oracle.js:223 `factHasText(el) && el.inactiveText !== true`) but never to its independently-authored cross-check (coverage-registry.js:37 `when: (el) => factHasText(el)`). Rule 16 requires familiesFor(el) to be a SUPERSET of the registry's demand, so ANY page containing a text-bearing element that is disabled/aria-disabled — or a <label> whose control is disabled — produces a coverage error, and build-v3.js:86 then returns { ok:false, results:null }: no obligations, no shadow observations, no LLM judging, for EVERY SC on that page. Confirmed by re-running coverageErrors over all 405 corpus pages: 8 pages abort, every one of them scored noObligation, and every abort is this same missing text-contrast family. 6 of the 8 are expected:failed, i.e. 6 run-wide FNs from a one-line drift.
patterns.proposedFix: coverage-registry.js:37 -> `when: (el) => factHasText(el) && el.inactiveText !== true`. Add a fixture with a <fieldset disabled> / <button aria-disabled> that asserts built.ok === true. Independently, downgrade a per-element coverage gap from a total build abort to a recorded error that still publishes the rest of the ledger — the current fail-closed is so blunt that a single-family disagreement silences 20+ unrelated SCs, which is itself a false-clear risk (the page reports nothing rather than reporting a gap).
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 in this bucket; 6 run-wide FNs (the other 3 are aug-2.1.2-input-gate-required-interaction-exception-case-03, aug-4.1.3-removal-of-status-conveys-meaning-silently-case-06, aug-4.1.3-announced-text-lacks-visual-context-case-04)

patterns.name: 1.4.13 Rule-15 applicability observer still uses the pre-generalization trigger definition, so a PROVEN barrier is demoted and the LLM is then locked out
patterns.description: This is the most damaging defect I found, because it INVERTS the harness: for 1.4.13, the deterministic runner SUCCEEDING is what causes the miss. hover-content-tri declares only a BARRIER_OBSERVED support, so proposer.js:33 emits a proposal ONLY when a barrier is proven. The builder then requires channel agreement with the independent observer (build-v3.js:196), whose hover-trigger definition is still the old tooltip-library one: applicability-observer.js:33 `hasTrigger = el.hasAttribute('title') || el.hasAttribute('aria-describedby')`. The runner meanwhile hardcodes `hasTrigger: hasTitle || hasDesc || true` (exp-runners.js:1402), i.e. always true. Therefore the two flags can agree ONLY when the element carries title or aria-describedby — and the round-3 overfit-audit fix #2 deliberately generalized the collector to nominate CSS-:hover and JS-toggled reveals that by construction have neither. Every such proven barrier becomes a deterministic PARTIAL, and build-v3.js:600 then skips the LLM PROVISIONAL fill because 'a CLAIM/PARTIAL already owns it' -> inScopeAutoPartial = 0 -> outcome noObligation. Cases where the runner FAILS to measure produce no proposal, stay auto-PARTIAL, and get judged by the LLM (which is how the other 17 1.4.13 cases were caught). So the generalization that was meant to recover this lane is exactly what the observer kills.
patterns.proposedFix: Primary: bring applicability-observer.js:33 in line with act-page-collect.js:321-327 (popovertarget / aria-describedby|aria-controls -> tooltip|popover / inline hover-focus handler attribute / CSS :hover|:focus reveal rule with a tail), or simply remove 'hasHoverFocusTrigger' from OBSERVED_FLAGS (applicability-observer.js:50) since the runner's value is a constant and the flag carries zero corroboration value. Belt and braces: extend the 2.1.2 precedence carve-out at build-v3.js:520-532 so a bind-failed PARTIAL never blocks the §5b PROVISIONAL fill — an unbound barrier should fall through to the LLM, not silence the obligation.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 in this bucket directly; structurally it un-blocks the whole generalized 1.4.13 lane and is a PREREQUISITE for the collector-blind fix below (fixing the collector alone would just feed 4 more proven barriers into the same demotion)

patterns.name: hasHoverContent is a static scan and cannot see addEventListener-wired reveals
patterns.description: act-page-collect.js:321-327 detects hover candidacy from four static signals: popovertarget, aria-describedby/aria-controls pointing at an existing [role=tooltip]/[popover], an INLINE on* attribute from a fixed list (mouseover/mouseenter/pointerover/pointerenter/focus/focusin — note: no mousemove), or a stylesheet :hover/:focus rule with a non-empty tail after the pseudo. All four of these pages use addEventListener, which the comment at :283-285 already concedes is invisible. Two of them are additionally adversarial about the static signals: case-02 of applicability-author-vs-ua DELETES the title attribute at load, and case-05 creates its role=tooltip element in script AFTER the collector's _tooltipIds scan. Because the lane is barrier-only, over-nomination costs only a probe, so this can be widened aggressively.
patterns.proposedFix: Install an addEventListener monkey-patch via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument BEFORE page scripts run, recording which elements register mouseenter/mouseover/mousemove/pointerenter/pointerover/focus/focusin, and read it back in the collect pass (alternatively DOMDebugger.getEventListeners over the candidate set). Also add 'mousemove'/'pointermove' to _HOVER_FOCUS_HANDLER_ATTRS and re-scan _tooltipIds after hydration. Must ship together with the applicability-observer fix above or it recovers nothing.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 4 in this bucket (all 6 of the run's 1.4.13 failed/noObligation cases are in this bucket, so these two 1.4.13 patterns together cover all of them)

patterns.name: backgroundImageMeaningful nominates only text-free carriers of at least 16x16
patterns.description: act-page-collect.js:678-679 requires the bg-image carrier to have `text.length === 0 && _accName.length === 0`, and (unless interactive) `box.width >= 16 && box.height >= 16`. Those two conjuncts exclude the two commonest real F3 shapes: an informative bg-image layered next to an element's own prose (F3 Example 1 — case-01's APR badge; case-06's exit-row glyph on a seat button labelled '12A'), and a sub-16px required/status marker glyph (case-03's 12x12 red asterisk spans). The comment immediately above the gate already argues that informational-vs-decorative is the RUBRIC's call, not the collector's, and that letting the collector cap by size created a silent FN — the same argument applies to the text-free conjunct, which was never revisited.
patterns.proposedFix: Drop the `text.length === 0` conjunct (keep `_accName.length === 0`, which is the real redundancy signal) and lower the size floor to a tracking-pixel test (>= 2x2) — or exempt bg-images inside a <label>/control from the floor. The barrier-only alt-text-adequacy / decorative-image-verification rubrics already own the redundancy judgment. Validate on the official ACT subset before shipping, since this widens a high-volume family.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 in this bucket (case-06 additionally needs the coverage-abort fix); run-wide 1.1.1 has 3 failed/noObligation, all of them here

patterns.name: P1 - F46 layout-table fabrication is structurally unreachable
patterns.description: The deterministic table gate resolves all six to a hard do-not-flag: case-01/04/06 => VALID (a scope= or a resolving headers= is present, llm-adjudicator.js:592-594); case-02/03 => NOT_DATA/NO_DATA_TABLE (looksLikeDataTable requires rows>1, collect-tables.js:96); case-05 has no native <table> at all so tables[] is empty. The gate answers 'is the header ASSOCIATION wired correctly' and the rubric converts that answer into a clearance for the ENTIRE table facet - but F46's question is the opposite one, 'should this table have data semantics at all'. In every case the wiring is flawless BECAUSE the author copied data-table markup onto page chrome. axe cannot backstop this: axe-core 4.10.3 has no `layout-table` rule (verified by string scan of the bundled axe.min.js).
patterns.proposedFix: Split the table facet in two. (a) Collect `summary` (currently dropped entirely) and add a `layoutTableSmell` fact: a table carrying th/caption/summary whose cells contain landmarks, navs, headings or forms rather than tabular data. (b) Add an F46 clause to info-relationships-v0, and scope the VALID/NOT_DATA gate so it suppresses only the header-ASSOCIATION barrier, never the layout-vs-data barrier. (c) Add an ARIA-role structural inventory so case-05's role=table grid is visible at all.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: up to 6 cases (5 confidently; case-03 depends on treating an obsolete `summary` as a real barrier and case-06 is mild)

patterns.name: P2 - the 'never fail the INVERTED direction' rule over-generalises
patterns.description: info-relationships-v0.md:115-122 and 213-215 tell the judge that 1.3.1's mismatch direction is VISUAL -> PROGRAMMATIC only and that 'if the only mismatch you can name runs programmatic->visual, return NOT REPRODUCED'. That rule was written for a narrow, correct purpose (an sr-only <h1> is a conforming technique, not a failure) but it is stated as a blanket prohibition. It therefore also forbids the entire FABRICATED-RELATIONSHIP family - F46 layout tables, headings on non-heading text (H42), blockquote on non-quotations, dl on non-term/description pairs - where markup asserts a relationship the content does not have. This is the single most load-bearing rubric line in the bucket: 9 of 21 cases are structurally cleared by it.
patterns.proposedFix: Narrow the caveat to its actual purpose: 'a programmatic structure that is VISUALLY HIDDEN is not a failure'. Then add an explicit third direction to the Judge paragraph: 'markup that asserts a relationship the content does not have (a data-table role over page chrome, a heading over a byline, a quotation over first-party prose, a term/description pair over independent spec lines) is ALSO a 1.3.1 failure.'
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 9 cases unblocked (overlaps P1; the incremental gain over P1 alone is the 3 structural-markup cases)

patterns.name: P3 - info-relationships-v0 has no control-semantics facet (F42/F59)
patterns.description: WCAG F42 fails 1.3.1 (and 2.1.1) for scripting-emulated links/buttons, but the rubric's enumerated facets are headings, heading level, table association, lists and groups - nothing about roles or controls. All four judge summaries dutifully report 'heading hierarchy fine, no data tables, no faux lists' on pages whose entire defect is a role-less control: pagination, a clickable , an submit button, and role-less div tabs. There is also no collector fact to work from: nothing inventories elements that behave/render as controls but carry no role.
patterns.proposedFix: Collect a `pseudoControls[]` signal (element has a click/keydown handler OR cursor:pointer OR link/button/tab styling, AND has no role, AND is not a natively interactive tag) and add a corresponding facet to info-relationships-v0. Route the composite widget shapes (tablist, accordion) through it too, since the selected/expanded STATE is part of the visually-conveyed relationship.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 4 cases

patterns.name: P4 - no faux-TABLE / space-formatted-column detector (F34/F32)
patterns.description:
collect-lists.js nominates faux LISTS from leading-marker text (kind:'faux'), and the rubric has a clause for judging them - but there is no analogue for faux TABLES or COLUMNS built from space padding in 
 / white-space:pre. signals.structure.tables[] is native--only, so both pages report NO_DATA_TABLE and the judge has nothing to look at. The 1.3.2 lane cannot backstop case-03 either, because 'meaningful-sequence' is gated on a VSR visual-vs-DOM order divergence (applicability-oracle.js:64) and a single 
 produces none.
patterns.proposedFix: Add a faux-column/faux-table candidate: a monospace or white-space:pre block with >=3 lines each containing >=2 runs of 3+ consecutive spaces at consistent column offsets. Emit it as a CANDIDATE (same contract as kind:'faux' lists) and route it to both 1.3.1 (F34) and 1.3.2 (F32). Precision assist: a candidate whose surrounding prose names a column ('the STATUS column', 'the same row's READY') is near-certain.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases

patterns.name: P5 - no styling-outlier signal for 'emphasis that carries meaning' (F2)
patterns.description: 'an emphasis that carries meaning' appears exactly once, in the rubric's Judge sentence (info-relationships-v0.md:91-93), and then never again: it has no entry in the 'Common failure patterns' list, no collected signal, and no detection guidance. signals.structure carries headings/landmarks/tables/lists only - no computed font-weight/size/variant facts - so the judge would have to spot a font-weight difference in a downscaled viewport screenshot unaided, with no tool for querying styling outliers. All three judge summaries correctly enumerate the (genuinely clean) headings/lists/tables and stop.
patterns.proposedFix: Collect `styleOutliers[]`: text runs whose computed font-weight / font-size / font-variant-caps / font-style differ from their sibling peers in the same repeated component, where the difference is NOT accompanied by any text or markup difference. Add an F2 clause that judges whether the outlier marks a status/category. Precision guard (special-status case-05 is a deliberate trap): require the outlier to recur in the SAME structural slot across >=2 repeated components, so a one-off decorative bold does not fire.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases, but see notes - this family is the most likely to contain corpus defects

patterns.name: P6 - field-programmatic-association judged from source, not from the crops it was given
patterns.description: All 15 field-programmatic-association verdicts in this bucket are LIKELY_OK/high and every single one reduces to 'a matching <label for> / id pair exists'. None engages clause 2 (table-context association), clause 3 (graphical-cue-only required/format marker), or the visual POSITION of the label relative to the field - even though the rubric hands the judge an element-crop and a surrounding-region precisely for that. The failure is uniform across three quite different defects: a CSS-grid label/input swap (case-01, where the crop plainly shows 'MM / DD / YYYY' under 'Number of guests'), colour-only required marking (case-03), and an unassociated group question (case-05). The rubric asks the right question at L22-23 but its three enumerated shapes let a judge answer it with an attribute check.
patterns.proposedFix: (a) Add a fourth failure shape: 'the programmatic association points at a DIFFERENT field than the visually adjacent label'. (b) Require a per-clause disposition in the verdict schema so clauses 2 and 3 cannot be silently skipped. (c) Give clauses 3 and 4 deterministic hooks - surface the field's required/aria-required state, the label's computed colour vs its siblings, and a label-box-vs-target-box proximity check that flags when a nearer field exists.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2-3 cases (case-01 confidently; case-03 likely; case-05 contested)

patterns.name: P7 - no axe 1.3.1 signal can reach the page-level 1.3.1 judge (plumbing, low yield here)
patterns.description: Three independent filters block it. (1) build-v3.js:316-321 deliberately omits 1.3.1 from AXE_SC_FAMILY, so an axe 1.3.1 violation never fills an obligation ('1.3.1 is deliberately NOT remapped ... those stay shadow checker signals'); build-v3.js:330 additionally drops anything with review:true. (2) orchestrator.js:425 builds checkerHints ONLY from kind:'incomplete' findings, so a review:true axe VIOLATION (heading-order, region, page-has-heading-one) reaches neither the barrier lane nor the hint lane - it is surfaced into checkerFindings and then goes nowhere. (3) Hints are keyed by exact xpath (orchestrator.js:426) and additionally require an SC match (llm-adjudicator.js:975), so an element-level axe node can never match the synthetic page-level subject `/page-level::info-relationships` (applicability-oracle.js:167). MEASURED YIELD IS SMALL: I ran axe 4.10.3 over all 21 pages. Only three produced a 1.3.1-relevant decided signal - `heading-order` on structural-markup case-01, `aria-prohibited-attr` (incomplete, 4.1.2) on emulated-controls case-05, and `label-title-only` on form-label case-05 (which axe-surface discards entirely: not in BEST_PRACTICE_RULE_SC and no wcag tag). Everything else was color-contrast or the region/landmark-one-main best-practice advisories. So this is a real plumbing gap but NOT the driver of the 1.3.1 recall gap.
patterns.proposedFix: (a) Let review:true axe violations become checkerHints alongside kind:'incomplete'. (b) For a PAGE-LEVEL subject, join hints by SC over the whole page rather than by exact xpath, passing the element selector along as context. (c) Add `label-title-only` to BEST_PRACTICE_RULE_SC (sc 1.3.1, review:true). Do NOT promote any of these to authoritative barriers - heading-order is advisory (G141) and would over-fire.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 0-1 cases directly; the value is diagnostic (the judge would at least be pointed at the right element)

patterns.name: 1.4.1 aperture is links + form fields only
patterns.description: applicability-oracle.js:313 is the ENTIRE 1.4.1 applicability rule: `if (role === 'link' || el.isFormField === true || FORMFIELD_ROLE.test(role)) fams.push('use-of-color')`. Every colour-only barrier that lives outside those two element classes — colour-keyed chart/map legends, error-summary rows, CPK/route colour encodings, a green 'saved' table row — mints ZERO obligations, so the judge is handed a set of irrelevant inputs and correctly clears each one. In all 5 cases the obligation list contains no element within reach of the defect. This ALSO explains the run's 5 1.4.1 FALSE POSITIVES: every FP in bucket H is likewise on a link or a form field. The lane is aimed at a narrow aperture, is trigger-happy inside it (three FPs are the judge flagging an F73 link that the corpus deliberately built as an inapplicability/escape-hatch boundary, one computing 'contrast ratio 1.62' it cannot measure from a crop), and asks nothing outside it. Over-firing and under-firing are the same defect: the aperture is both too narrow and too weakly instrumented.
patterns.proposedFix: Add ONE collector fact and gate on it: `colorDifferentiatedPeer` — this element's computed color/background/border/stroke/fill differs from its structurally-identical same-role peers (same tag+depth, or sibling SVG shapes identical in every presentational attribute but fill/stroke), plus the legend shape (a container whose children each pair a solid-colour swatch with a text label). That single predicate covers all five FNs and is bounded — it only fires where a peer set exists, so it cannot flood.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 5 cases in this bucket; likely more across the 1.4.1 stratum

patterns.name: The 1.1.1 decorative lane exists but its redundancy evidence is contaminated or absent
patterns.description: ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S STRUCTURAL QUESTION: the harness CAN flag 'this was wrongly marked decorative'. applicability-oracle.js:292-298 deliberately routes unnamed removed-from-tree images to decorative-image-verification-v0 (the decorativeSuspect lane), and it DID fire on the correct element in both suppressed-image cases where the image was large enough. So this is NOT a structural blind spot in the way feared. The lane fails on its EVIDENCE, in two opposite ways. (a) Contaminated: nearbyText is textOf(el.parentElement) (act-page-collect.js:607-613, textOf = innerText||textContent), which for an inline SVG INCLUDES the SVG's own suppressed <text> — so the redundancy test the whole rubric turns on self-satisfies. Probe on the dosing case returned nearbyText = 'Morning 2 tablets Midday 1 tablet Night 1 tablet TAKE WITH FOOD ...', i.e. verbatim the aria-hidden content it was supposed to be compared against. Compounding this, llm-adjudicator.js:350 ships svgLiveText with the steer 'its text is REAL and machine-readable' and no removedFromA11yTree guard — for an aria-hidden SVG that statement is simply false. (b) Absent: for the canvas case nearbyText was undefined (empty parent), and the judge invented a 'real HTML table visible in the surrounding region' rather than returning the PARTIAL its own rubric mandates.
patterns.proposedFix: (1) act-page-collect.js:610 — clone the parent, remove the element, then take text, so nearbyText means text OUTSIDE the image. (2) llm-adjudicator.js:350 — gate svgLiveText on removedFromA11yTree !== true and emit the inverse steer when the subtree is hidden. (3) decorative-image-verification-v0 — make empty/null nearbyText a MANDATORY PARTIAL, and forbid crediting redundancy against content visible only inside the element crop.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases here; the nearbyText contamination is systemic for every inline-SVG decorative judgment

patterns.name: The genuine 1.1.1 applicability blind spot: sub-24px status badges
patterns.description: The narrow version of the design flaw the brief asked about. decorativeSuspect() (applicability-oracle.js:138-161) requires minDim >= 24px, or an aspect >= 4 elongated strip. A verification checkmark, a 'New' pill, a warning glyph — precisely the class of image whose PRESENCE-vs-ABSENCE is itself the datum — is typically 16-22px and square, so it fails both escapes and is dropped silently. The MarketNest badge measures 22x22: it misses by 2 pixels. The size floor is defensible for spacers but it is inversely correlated with the badge/status failure mode, where information density per pixel is highest.
patterns.proposedFix: Keep the 24px floor as the default but add a context escape: a removed-from-tree image below the floor is still a suspect when it sits inside a small inline/flex row alongside text (or matches a badge/status/icon class or an SVG containing only a filled circle + a check/cross path). Cost is bounded: such elements are rare relative to the spacer population the floor is defending against.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here; the badge shape is likely common across the meaningful-image-suppressed rule family

patterns.name: long-description-completeness is never handed the long description
patterns.description: long-description-completeness-v0.md:32-35 states the judge is handed 'the text alternative (short alt AND any long description / caption / associated text region)'. It is not. nearbyText is surfaced only inside s.decorativeMarking (llm-adjudicator.js:403-409), which is built only for removed-from-tree images, and no aria-describedby / figcaption resolution exists anywhere else in buildSignals. For an IN-tree complex image the judge gets crops and an alt string and must read the caption off a screenshot. Two of the three cases said so verbatim ('Cannot determine ... without inspecting the referenced element's content'; 'Could not verify ... without querying the accessibility node') and abstained to auto-PARTIAL; the third confabulated that a flat roster caption 'conveys ... reporting relationships'. All three pages are genuine F67 failures with a plausible-but-incomplete long description, which is exactly what this rubric exists to catch.
patterns.proposedFix: Add a `longDescription` signal for any element with complexImageHint: resolve aria-describedby target ids, enclosing figcaption, <details>, and an adjacent data table to TEXT, and hand it over with a 'compare this text to the pixels' steer. Add a structure checklist to the rubric: name the relation the image encodes (edges / branches / interchanges / hierarchy), then verify that relation appears in the text — a roster of the nodes is insufficient by construction.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases here; whole complex-image-long-description-incomplete family

patterns.name: The declared 1.4.1 required tool is never invoked
patterns.description: required-tool-routing.js:10 declares render_with_overrides(grayscale) as REQUIRED evidence for SC 1.4.1, and the tool is fully implemented (cdp-tools.js:801-828, CDP Emulation.setEmulatedVisionDeficiency, catalog cdp-tool-catalog.js:43-44). But grep for requiredToolFor / REQUIRED_TOOL_ROUTING across scripts/ finds NO consumer — the module's own header says 'the runner/orchestrator SHOULD invoke', and the only force-invoke that actually shipped is the hard-coded 2.4.4 resolve_destination at orchestrator.js:357. Both cases here are the judge abstaining with an explicit request for the render it never received. Compounding: use-of-color-v0.md:61-64 already forbids applying the grayscale/lightness escape to F81 red=invalid states, so the judge should have returned REPRODUCED without any render — it invoked the very escape the rubric's CRITICAL GUARD rules out, then abstained on not having it.
patterns.proposedFix: Wire required-tool-routing generically the way 2.4.4 is wired: for each obligation, look up requiredToolFor(sc), force-invoke, attach as required evidence. Add one line to use-of-color-v0: 'never abstain pending a grayscale/CVD render on an F81 state — the guard above already makes contrast irrelevant there'. Cheapest recovery in the bucket.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases here; plus likely FP reduction, since 1.4.5/1.4.3/1.4.11 routing is equally unenforced

patterns.name: The text-lookalike detector exists but is a signal, not a gate
patterns.description: confusable-text.js is a well-built detector covering math-styled, fullwidth, enclosed, homoglyph-mix and homoglyph-full, with a lang-aware exemption. It is consumed ONLY at llm-adjudicator.js:236, i.e. as an extra signal on elements that ALREADY carry an obligation. The applicability gate for the glyph lane is a separate, much narrower ad-hoc regex at act-page-collect.js:621 (PUA codepoints, or Cyrillic/Greek AND Latin in the same text). Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols (U+1D400-1D7FF) fall in neither branch, and a pure-Cyrillic run with no surviving Latin letter fails the mix test. Verified by probe: both pages return hasGlyphText=false on every defective element, while detectConfusableText returns hasConfusables=true with asciiFold='Sumi Tanaka' for one of them. There is also no glyph-text-alternative-v0.md rubric in scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/, so the family (applicability-oracle.js:79, catalog.js:178) may have no rubric to route to even once it fires.
patterns.proposedFix: Replace the act-page-collect.js:621 regex with `detectConfusableText(ownText, nearestLang).hasConfusables` — the module is already loaded in the same process and already tested (scripts/v3/tests/runners/confusable-text.test.js covers exactly these shapes). Then confirm/author the rubric the glyph-text-alternative family routes to. Separately reconsider confusable-text.js:94's `letters.length >= 4` floor for currency/digit-adjacent tokens ('$ЗОО' is 3 letters).
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases here; the whole text-lookalike-glyph-substitution rule family

patterns.name: use-of-color-v0 answers a narrower question than SC 1.4.1 asks
patterns.description: In these three the obligations landed on exactly the right elements and the judge's pixel observations were mostly correct — the rubric's taxonomy is just incomplete. Three missing clauses, each a distinct 1.4.1 shape: (a) CATEGORY BY HUE — peers of the same role split into classes by colour alone (teal = opens in a new tab vs blue = same window); the rubric only knows link-vs-prose and widget-state, so all ten verdicts answered 'is this link underlined?' and missed the actual datum. (b) SHARED CUE — the F73 clause credits 'distinct weight' without requiring the cue be link-SPECIFIC, so a theme that styles <strong> identically to <a> (verified: both rgb(157,27,61)/700/none) passes despite no visual link affordance existing. (c) STATIC-INSTRUCTION-AS-STATE-CUE — a permanent describedby hint accepted as the non-colour cue for a live error state. Aggravating all three: the judge fabricates cue observations in BOTH directions (a non-existent underline in the FN case-05; precise 'contrast ratio 1.62 / 2.87:1 / 3.91:1' numbers in the FP cases that no crop supports).
patterns.proposedFix: Three rubric clauses: category-by-hue as a third failure mode alongside F73/F81; 'the non-colour cue must be UNIQUE to the class within its block'; 'the non-colour cue must be STATE-DEPENDENT — would this text also be present in the pass state?'. Structurally better: micro-checks.js:132-142 already contains `use-of-color-adequacy`, a per-cue boolean sibling-comparison check that the header records as winning two prompt bake-offs with 'lowest false-clears and ZERO false-barriers', plus a `use-of-color-state` variant at :147. Both are DEAD in the v3 path — runInteractionChecklist (their only caller, interaction-checklist.js:32) is referenced nowhere in scripts/, only by two validators under eval/capability-tests/_tools/. Routing 1.4.1 obligations through that per-cue check instead of the free-form rubric would address the fabricated-cue problem on both the FP and FN side at once.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases here, and plausibly several of the run's 5 1.4.1 false positives

patterns.name: 3.3.1 semantic-consistency gap (message is fluent, field-naming, and factually wrong)
patterns.description: error-identification-v0.md judges PRESENCE and SPECIFICITY of error text but never its TRUTH. Its only enumerated failure modes are no-text/colour-only and the AMBIGUOUS-FIELD shared-label case. Every one of these pages renders the post-submit error state statically at rest (aria-invalid + associated message already in the DOM, no script), so the evidence was fully in hand - the judge simply had no clause telling it to compare the message against the retained value or against constraints the page itself states. All six cleared at high confidence.
patterns.proposedFix: Add a REPRODUCED clause: 'Cross-check the message against the field's RETAINED VALUE and any constraint the page states (hint text, policy copy, a requirements checklist, aria-describedby text). If it names a cause the value does not exhibit, demands a format the value already satisfies, or quotes a value the field does not contain, the actual error is not described in text => REPRODUCED.' Cheap, purely prompt-side, and the highest-yield single edit in this bucket.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 6 cases

patterns.name: 4.1.3 announced-content adequacy gap (rubric judges plumbing, never the string)
patterns.description: status-message-v0.md asks only whether the update reaches AT through an appropriately-marked, pre-existing live region without moving focus. It never asks whether the announced phrase, standing alone, conveys the status. Confirmed by live VSR probe: the instrument returned exactly ['polite: 1'], bare percentages, and ['assertive: ''] - correct observations that the judge read as passes.
patterns.proposedFix: Add: 'Read liveRegionAnnouncements. Ask whether the PHRASE ALONE carries the status a sighted user gets from the visual change. A bare number/percentage/symbol, an empty phrase, or a phrase missing the subject that visual adjacency supplies does NOT convey the status => REPRODUCED.'
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases

patterns.name: 4.1.3 obligation is keyed on el.liveRegion===true, so a status in a NON-live element has no subject
patterns.description: applicability-oracle.js:241 mints status-message only for elements the collector already marked as live regions. The canonical 4.1.3 barrier - a success/outcome panel swapped in as a plain <div> - is therefore structurally unreachable. When the page also has an innocent correctly-wired region (the 'loading' one), the case scores missedAgree rather than noObligation, hiding the gate problem. This same blind spot likely inflates the 18 noObligation 4.1.3 cases in the run summary.
patterns.proposedFix: Mint a status-message obligation for text that becomes visible after an activation and lands OUTSIDE any live region. observe_state_after_activation already computes exactly this (cdp-tools.js:521-523: newlyVisibleNodes with inLiveRegion / liveRegionPreExisted). Also treat 'a busy/loading region is emptied with no successor announcement' as a first-class barrier signal.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases here; likely more among the 18 4.1.3 noObligation FNs

patterns.name: Fabricated native constraint-validation messages
patterns.description: Both pages are novalidate with NO required/pattern/type constraint on any field; headless Chrome confirms form.checkValidity()===true and validationMessage==='' for every input, before and after clearing. Yet the judge cleared obligations by quoting invented browser messages - 'Veuillez remplir ce champ.', 'Veuillez sélectionner l'un de ces boutons radio.', 'Please fill in this field.' The prompt-level cause is the rubric's own strongly-worded nativeDialogText paragraph, which trains the judge to believe in error text that the screenshots provably cannot show; the model then supplies it. The French strings are a second tell: Chrome localises validation text to the BROWSER locale, not the page's lang.
patterns.proposedFix: In error-identification-v0.md: 'You may cite a native validation/dialog message ONLY if it appears VERBATIM in a tool result (signals.nativeDialogText or invalidFields[].validationMessage); name the field it came from. If no such field is listed, no native message exists. A native message rendered in the PAGE's language rather than the browser's is evidence of fabrication.' Consider also having the harness pass an explicit 'nativeConstraintValidation: none (form novalidate / no constrained fields)' signal so absence is stated, not inferred.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case directly (the colour-only bistro page); the other needs the redisplay clause too

patterns.name: Empty live-region announcements read as evidence of announcing
patterns.description: Every 'region emptied on completion' page yields a trailing 'polite: ' / 'assertive: ' entry. cdp-tools.js:692 keeps them (filter(Boolean) on the prefixed string) and :697 counts them as liveRegionAnnouncements, so noLiveRegionAnnouncement is FALSE and announcementCount is non-zero even though the user hears nothing. The judge reads a non-empty queue as 'it announces'.
patterns.proposedFix: Strip the 'polite: '/'assertive: ' prefix before the emptiness test and expose emptyPhraseCount / nonEmptyLiveRegionAnnouncements. Rubric: an empty phrase is silence, and the state to judge is the TERMINAL one, not an intermediate loading phrase.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1-2 cases on its own; a necessary enabler for the other two 4.1.3 patterns

patterns.name: The screen-reader instrument is aria-atomic-blind
patterns.description: Verified directly against scripts/v3/lib/vsr-collect.js on the live page: for p#result-count (role=status, NO aria-atomic) where only the inner <b> numeral is rewritten, the VSR voices the ENTIRE region - 'polite: النتائج: ٦ نتيجة'. Real AT would announce only the changed node. This is a false-CLEARING instrument defect, not merely a missing observation, and it will suppress every non-atomic partial-update case in the corpus. It also means VSR output must not be trusted as ground truth for announcement CONTENT on non-atomic regions in either direction.
patterns.proposedFix: Compose the reported announcement per the ARIA live-region algorithm (changed node + ancestors up to an aria-atomic='true' ancestor) inside probe_screen_reader_after_action and expose an atomicityTruncated flag; or add a deterministic detector for 'live region text mutation confined to a descendant while aria-atomic is absent/false'.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here; systemic across the SC

patterns.name: 2.4.3 page-level focus-order is judged with ZERO evidence
patterns.description: focus-order-meaning-v0 opens by telling the judge that 'the deterministic tab-order instrument already WALKED the page and RECORDED the focus SEQUENCE' and that the sequence plus a state-before/state-after pair are 'handed to you'. None of that is true. (1) collectTabOrder DOES compute the ordered list, but run-instruments.js:62 keeps only tabOrderFindings(tab).findings and throws tab.order away. (2) The subject is the synthetic xpath /page-level::focus-order, which resolves to no element, so selectRubricSubjects builds the bare stub {xpath} — and focus-management is NOT in PAGE_STRUCTURE_SKILLS (llm-adjudicator.js:149), so unlike 2.4.2/1.3.1 it gets no page-structure thread either. Verified: precomputeSignals returns {rawElementHtml:null, enclosingHtml:null}. (3) STATE_TRANSITIONS (vision-capture.js:126) has no '2.4.3' entry, so the declared state pair is never captured; the required-evidence gate that should then ABSTAIN is bypassed because the unresolvable xpath is flagged __nonVisual='1', which routes the subject to the 'judge text-only, do NOT return PARTIAL just because you cannot see' path. (4) The 2.4.3 tool set is only set_state_and_capture + capture_full_page — interact_and_observe (the only key-pressing tool) is not offered for 2.4.3, so the judge cannot recover the order itself. Net effect: the model is handed one above-the-fold screenshot and a rubric asserting it has a tab sequence, and it confabulates one — all six verdicts are LIKELY_OK with fabricated sequence descriptions ('nav, hero CTA, menu items in sequence, then footer'; 'focus returns to the modal after a brief visit to the cookie banner'). This is the systemic cause of the 2.4.3 collapse the brief asked about, and it also explains the 17 sibling `uncertain` verdicts.
patterns.proposedFix: Thread collectTabOrder's `order` (index/xpath/tag/label/rect + wrapped/exhausted flags) into the /page-level::focus-order subject as a deterministic signal with an uncertainReason ('this is the recorded sequence; absence of a divergence finding is NOT a pass'), and either add focus-management to PAGE_STRUCTURE_SKILLS or add an equivalent focus-order thread. Until the sequence exists, the honest behaviour is to ABSTAIN, not judge: do not let __nonVisual bypass the required-evidence gate for a page-level subject whose evidence is non-visual by design.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases outright from the resting sequence alone (both nested-focusable cases + the modal); the other 3 need the reveal pathway below

patterns.name: The F85 reveal-then-check-focus-order runner is dead code
patterns.description: reveal-state-runner.js:73-88 implements exactly this failure ('a <role> opened but focus was NOT moved into it (F85): focus stayed on the trigger' => verdict fail). Nothing ever requests it: a repo-wide grep for 'reveal-then-check-focus-order' hits only its own implementation, and runReveal is called from exactly one place (exp-runners.js:1611) with a different aspect. runRevealChecklist (reveal-checklist.js) is exported but imported by no production module. So a deterministic detector for the precise defect shape of these three cases exists and never runs.
patterns.proposedFix: Emit a reveal experiment request for every disclosure trigger the collector sees (aria-haspopup / aria-expanded / a click handler toggling a class on a role=dialog|menu|listbox region), with triggerSelector + revealedSelector, and route it to the existing runner. All three cases have aria-haspopup + aria-expanded on the trigger, so the applicability signal is already collected.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 3 cases (and it would be a deterministic barrier, not a shadow LLM verdict)

patterns.name: 2.4.4 never compares a link's name against its actual destination
patterns.description: link-purpose-v0 enumerates three failure modes, all of which test whether the NAME IS VAGUE (format-only/action-only, generic-in-context, identical-names-different-destinations). There is no clause for a SPECIFIC name that names the WRONG destination, so a well-formed descriptive name is an automatic clear — reinforced by knowledge-layer principle 3 ('a requirement that is literally MET is not a barrier'). The judge is not evidence-starved here: 2.4.4 is outside HTML_RUNNER_OWNED_SC, so rawElementHtml carries the literal Read our Privacy Policy. It simply is never asked the question. The fifth case of this rule (case-02) scored 'caught' but for the WRONG reason — the judge cleared the actual defect (skip link 'Skip to main content' -> href=#site-footer) and instead flagged 'Apply'/'Renew' as action-only names — so the true detection rate on this defect shape is 0/5. resolve_destination cannot close the gap for these on-page-fragment links: it fingerprints the destination DOCUMENT (title/h1/first paragraph/visibleText, cdp-tools.js:1220-1232), so #privacy and #terms are byte-identical.
patterns.proposedFix: (a) Add a deterministic `fragmentTarget` signal for any same-page #fragment link: the target id's heading text / aria-label / nearest section name, plus a flag when two differently-named links resolve to the same id and when a plausible better-matching id exists. (b) Add a 'NAME CONTRADICTS DESTINATION' failure mode to link-purpose-v0 that judges name-vs-fragmentTarget. Both are cheap and cannot regress the vagueness judgments.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 4 cases here + the mis-credited case-02 = 5 on this rule

patterns.name: 2.4.2 judge inconsistency, esp. crediting title/h1 lexical overlap
patterns.description: These are NOT coverage gaps: the same rubric, in the same run, caught the identical shapes elsewhere ('Chapter 3' over h1 'Newton's Laws of Motion'; 'Settings' over h1 'Notification settings'; four wrong-instance titles including a version and a date). The discriminator on the two ordinal-title misses is pure string overlap with the h1: when the topicless title ('Exhibit B', 'Lámina 12') also happens to be the h1's LEADING TOKEN, the judge reads 'matches the visible content' as 'identifies the topic' — even though the title is exactly the h1 with its subject truncated away. 'Checkout' fails the same clause the judge applied to 'Settings'. The stale-gala miss most likely turned on the page's own retrospective 'Last year's Hope Gala (March 2025)' paragraph.
patterns.proposedFix: Two clauses in page-title-v0: (1) a title that is a TRUNCATED PREFIX of the h1, with the h1's subject removed, does not identify the topic — matching the h1's first token is not evidence; judge the retained fragment standalone. (2) extend the site-wide-constant clause to SECTION-wide constants across a multi-step flow, and the contradiction clause to WRONG-INSTANCE tokens (year/version/record id) within one subject family, noting that a retrospective mention of the sibling instance does not license a stale title.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 4 cases (2 high-confidence: Exhibit B, Lámina 12)

patterns.name: 2.4.3 focus-order lane never receives the tab sequence it is designed around
patterns.description: THE headline finding, and it is unambiguously evidence-gap, not missing-tool. The instrument exists and runs: scripts/v3/lib/kbd-graph.js:43-66 `collectTabOrder` drives real Tab keypresses from the top of the document until the ring wraps, recording {index, xpath, tag, rect, label} per stop, with explicit handling for the positive-tabindex ring boundary (lines 55-57). It is invoked on every page at scripts/v3/lib/run-instruments.js:61. But line 62 is `if (tab) add('tab-order', tabOrderFindings(tab).findings);` — only the DERIVED divergence findings are kept and `tab.order` itself is dropped on the floor. Grepping tab-order/tabOrder across llm-adjudicator.js, obligations.js, build-v3.js and judgments.js returns ZERO hits: the sequence reaches no judge in any form. Worse, the surviving findings are keyed to real element xpaths while the obligation is keyed to the synthetic `/page-level::focus-order` (applicability-oracle.js:170,362), so they could never join even in principle — and the same xpath mismatch blocks axe's positive-tabindex advisory prior (axe-surface.js:83) from reaching the judge via `checkerHintsByXpath[subj.xpath]`. The rubric meanwhile OPENS by promising the artifact — focus-order-meaning-v0.md:27-30, 'Evidence handed to you: the recorded tab-order SEQUENCE from the deterministic instrument (the ordered list of reached elements + any trap note)' — and line 49-50 instructs 'If the recorded sequence is empty/degenerate ... return PARTIAL rather than guessing.' So the judge was told to expect a sequence, given none, and told to abstain. It abstained, verbatim ('no recorded tab-sequence was supplied by the deterministic instrument'), in 17/17 cases. This is correct behaviour under a broken contract: the fix is to supply the evidence, NOT to loosen the rubric. `probe-case.js` settles every one of these 10 in seconds — e.g. css-reorder case-01 T1 = 'Place order & pay $48.00' at y=734 with T2 at y=0; f44 case-01 tabs Start then Modules 4,3,2,1 with monotonically decreasing y; multiple-valid case-06 tabs B3,A6,D1,A2,C5,... across a seat grid. The harness computes materially the same walk and then discards it.
patterns.proposedFix: In scripts/v3/lib/run-instruments.js:61-62, retain the sequence itself (not just findings) as a first-class instrument artifact, and surface it on the `/page-level::focus-order` subject's signals in llm-adjudicator.js as e.g. `signals.focusOrder = { forward: [{index, tag, label, rect, tabindex}], wrapped, exhausted }`. No new instrument, no new tool, no rubric edit — the rubric already documents this exact payload. Additionally aggregate page-scoped checker hints onto page-level subjects so the axe positive-tabindex prior stops dead-ending on element xpaths.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 10 cases directly; plausibly most of the 2.4.3 SC (20.0% recall, worst in the run)

patterns.name: Backward (Shift+Tab) walk is implemented but never invoked
patterns.description: kbd-graph.js already parameterises direction (`const backward = opts.backward === true`, line 44) and its file header states 'Forward AND backward (Shift+Tab) sequences are collected so a later trap/consistency check can compare directions.' run-instruments.js:61 calls `collectTabOrder(page)` with no options, so only the forward ring is ever walked. Any one-directional containment defect — a focus trap whose Shift+Tab branch was never written — is therefore invisible even to the deterministic lane. Cheapest fix in the bucket: one argument.
patterns.proposedFix: Add a second call `collectTabOrder(page, {backward:true})` in run-instruments.js and hand both sequences to the focus-order subject as `signals.focusOrder.{forward,backward}`.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here; generalises to every asymmetric-trap shape

patterns.name: interact_and_observe is not routed to 2.4.3, so post-interaction focus is unreachable
patterns.description: Six F85-shaped cases turn on where focus lands AFTER an interaction (dialog closed, menu opened), which no fresh-load sequence can answer — so passing tab.order through does not fix these. The right question is therefore whether an adequate tool exists, and it does: `interact_and_observe` accepts up to 16 primitive actions (click/press/focus/hover/drag) and returns per-step `revealedNow` and `activeAfter` — precisely [{op:click,xpath:trigger},{op:press,key:'Escape'}] then read activeAfter. But `toolsForSubject('2.4.3','focus-management')` resolves to ONLY [set_state_and_capture, capture_full_page]: interact_and_observe lists scs ['2.1.2','2.1.1','3.3.1','3.3.3','1.4.13'] and skills ['keyboard-operability','forms-instructions-errors','color-and-visual-text'], and the 2.4.3 subject carries skill 'focus-management' (applicability-oracle.js:61, rubric frontmatter), matching neither. Verified by executing toolsForSubject directly. So this is evidence-gap rather than missing-tool or tool-not-invoked: an adequate tool exists and the judge never declined to call it — the routing gate withheld it. Note the harness ALSO already drives the exact open/Escape cycle deterministically at reveal-state-runner.js:73-88 for the 'reveal-then-check-focus-order' aspect, and explicitly defers the residue to this rubric (line 86-87) — but hands over a prose uncertainReason rather than the observed focus targets.
patterns.proposedFix: Add '2.4.3' to interact_and_observe's scs (and/or 'focus-management' to its skills) in scripts/v3/lib/cdp-tool-catalog.js:25-27, with a 2.4.3 clause in its `when` text ('F85 focus return — click the trigger, press Escape, read step.activeAfter: focus back on the trigger or dropped to body?'). Complementarily, have reveal-state-runner.js emit the post-reveal/post-close activeElement and a post-reveal tab walk as structured evidence on the deferred obligation.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 6 cases

patterns.name: F91/F92 circularity — the table classifier reads the defect as proof of inapplicability
patterns.description: `tVerdict` in llm-adjudicator.js:588-590 computes `isData = looksLikeDataTable && roleOverride !== 'presentation' && roleOverride !== 'none'`, and `looksLikeDataTable` (collect-tables.js:96) requires `ths.length > 0 || caption`. The two canonical suppression failures are exactly the two conditions that make isData false: F91 removes every <th> (case-01: zero <th>, no caption) and F92 sets role='presentation' (case-04: a caption'd, fully scope'd timetable). Both collapse to NOT_DATA / NO_DATA_TABLE, whereupon info-relationships-v0.md:14-25 — 'a HARD GATE you may not override', 'perTable[i] = NOT_DATA ⇒ ... do NOT flag it' — forbids the judge from raising the barrier. Both judges said so explicitly in their summaries. The gate conflates 'no data semantics are PRESENT' with 'no data semantics are OWED'; whether a table owes associations is a question about its visual/semantic content, not about the markup whose absence is the defect.
patterns.proposedFix: Introduce a third disposition alongside NOT_DATA: SUPPRESSED, emitted when a table is geometrically a data grid (rows>1 && cols>1 && regularGrid) AND either carries zero header markup or has its semantics overridden by role=presentation/none while retaining real header markup. Route SUPPRESSED to the judge with the viewport (as UNCERTAIN already is) and add the rubric clause. Keep NOT_DATA for genuine layout tables (single row, or no grid geometry).
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases here; likely more across the 1.3.1 SC

patterns.name: CSS-derived hover triggers anchor to the wrapper tag, not the control
patterns.description: act-page-collect.js:290-318 mines stylesheets for reveal rules and extracts the trigger as the selector text BEFORE the pseudo-class (line 306: `const trigger = m[1].trim()`). For the extremely common menu idiom `li:hover > .submenu { display:block }` that trigger is the bare tag `li`, and `_hasHoverContent` then matches it with `el.matches(sel)` (line 325) against EVERY <li> on the page. Here that produced obligations on li[2] (Government) and li[3] (Business) — plain links with no submenu, which the judge correctly dismissed — while `<button id="svcToggle">`, the element that actually opens the panel on focus and click, matches 'li' not at all and received no obligation. The genuine dismissible failure (no Escape handler, no toggle-to-close, closes only on an outside pointer click) was therefore never put to any judge. Over-approximation was a deliberate design choice here (the code comment at line 288 argues a false candidate 'only costs a deterministic probe'), but it also MISSES the true anchor, which the comment does not anticipate.
patterns.proposedFix: When a reveal rule uses a descendant/child combinator, require the candidate to actually contain a subtree matching the revealed tail before setting hasHoverContent, and re-anchor the obligation to the nearest focusable descendant (the button) rather than the wrapper. This both removes the two spurious subjects and creates the missing real one.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here; the li:hover menu idiom is common enough that this likely recurs across the 1.4.13 SC

patterns.name: Required-evidence gate drops subjects silently, producing noVerdict
patterns.description: llm-adjudicator.js:1238 returns null when any rubric-declared vision frame is missing, which is a sound abstain policy but is INVISIBLE downstream — the obligation simply never yields a verdict and the case scores noVerdict with an empty rubricVerdicts array (2 obligations, 2 auto-partial, 0 verdicts here). The gate is also over-strict for page-level frames: `viewport` is assigned unconditionally at vision-capture.js:226 and is not element-dependent, yet it is looked up per-xpath via `visionByXpath[subj.xpath]`, so an xpath the capture pass never sampled yields avail={} and fails the gate even though a perfectly good page viewport exists. There is an unpleasant irony here: the most likely reason capture never sampled these xpaths is the focusin guard of the very trap under test.
patterns.proposedFix: (a) Emit an explicit abstain/dropped record instead of `return null`, so silent drops are observable in results.json; (b) for a rubric whose declared evidence is page-level (`viewport` only), fall back to the page viewport frame rather than requiring a per-element capture entry.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case here; the mechanism is generic and likely accounts for other noVerdict outcomes across the run

patterns.name: Static post-error redisplay cases are undecidable from the artifact
patterns.description:
Both cases assert a premise — 'the server rejected a submission and redisplayed the form' — that is not rendered anywhere in the static artifact. There is no server (the forms POST to /auth/login and /facilities/book), no client-side validation, and no observable trace of a prior attempt. 3.3.1 applies only when an input error IS automatically detected, so with the detection unobservable the SC cannot be evaluated. case-03's own metadata concedes 'the post-failure page is indistinguishable from a first, fresh visit'; case-01 goes further and renders as a SUCCESS confirmation ('Confirmation' breadcrumb, `

Request logged

`, 'Thanks — here are the details'), which contradicts the label, and its ruleName describes Age and Email fields the page does not contain (confirmed metadata drift). The judges' UNCERTAIN verdicts named the real obstacle ('the form appears to validate server-side and the real POST is blocked'). These are corpus defects, not harness misses.
patterns.proposedFix: Corpus-side: re-author so the rejection is observable in the artifact (an unambiguous failure heading with no per-field identification), or drive the case through a real POST. Harness-side no change is warranted — abstaining on an unobservable premise is correct.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 0 harness cases (2 corpus defects to remove from the denominator)

patterns.name: form-error-probe cannot credit an ALREADY-RENDERED error (errorStyled naming co-gate)
patterns.description: This single mechanism explains the ENTIRE 66.7% 3.3.1 FP rate — all four FPs, and zero LLM involvement (every 3.3.1 rubric verdict on these pages was UNCERTAIN or LIKELY_OK; the barriers are deterministic shadow observations). These corpus pages are STATIC snapshots of the post-submit error state with no validation JS. The probe ignores the error already on screen, synthesizes a NEW error on some field, submits, sees no NEW surface appear, and reports errorNotIdentified=true. The one path that could credit a pre-existing error (exp-runners.js:709) requires the aria-describedby target to ALSO pass errorStyled() — an error-ish role/class/id. Real pages name these things 'err', 'msg', 'field-msg', 'email-err'; ERR_CLASS requires the whole word 'error'. Proven by A/B on two different pages: changing ONE class token ('msg'->'msg error', 'err'->'error') and nothing else removes the barrier completely.
patterns.proposedFix: exp-runners.js:709 — drop the `&& errorStyled(n)` co-gate (a field's own aria-describedby/aria-errormessage target is associated error content by construction) and widen the unchanged-surface credit to `referencesField(n) || isLiveRegion(n)` so a pre-existing role=alert error summary with a[href='#fieldId'] also counts. Best framing: when the probed field is ALREADY in an error state (aria-invalid=true, or an associated error surface is already present), credit the existing identification instead of demanding a counterfactual re-validation.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 4 cases (all 3.3.1 FPs; 3.3.1 FP rate 66.7% -> 0%)

patterns.name: form-error-probe fabricates an error condition on optional type=tel fields
patterns.description: Independent second defect, verified by ablation. hasConstraint (exp-runners.js:588) counts bare `type=tel` as a constraint, but HTML defines no validation algorithm for tel. The probe then writes '' into an optional tel field — a VALID value — and flags the absence of an error message about a non-error. Deleting the phone field from case-06 drops it from 2 barriers to 1, with nothing else changed. Not the sole cause on either page, but it would keep both pages red even after the errorStyled fix.
patterns.proposedFix: Drop `tel` from the typed-constraint list at exp-runners.js:588, and/or gate the whole probe on the synthesized value actually being invalid (`!el.checkValidity()` post-mutation, or an author constraint that rejects it).
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 0 additional cases alone, but REQUIRED alongside the errorStyled fix for 2 of the 4

patterns.name: 1.4.1 F73 lane has no applicability precondition — 1:1 colour difference scores as maximally failing
patterns.description: SC 1.4.1 only engages when colour IS the means of conveying information. use-of-color-v0.md never asks that question; it goes straight to hunting for a non-colour affordance, with a >=3:1 link-vs-prose LIGHTNESS separation as the sole escape. A link styled identically to its prose has a 1:1 separation, so it fails the escape hardest — the SC is inverted, and links that use NO colour cue at all are flagged as colour-only failures. The judge's own summaries state the inversion out loud: 'shares the exact same color ... 1:1 contrast ratio' -> LIKELY_BARRIER. This is the same rubric that under-fires badly on recall (1.4.1: 8/29 = 27.6%), which is the classic signature of keying on the wrong feature rather than a mis-set threshold.
patterns.proposedFix: Add an applicability precondition at the top of the F73 bullet (use-of-color-v0.md:22): if link colour ~= prose colour (say <=1.1:1) and no other styling differs, colour is not the distinguishing means -> F73 inapplicable -> NOT REPRODUCED. Never treat a near-1:1 ratio as evidence of a colour-alone failure.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases

patterns.name: axe PASSES are discarded at collection, so the rubric's own DEFER clause is unreachable
patterns.description: HIGHEST-VALUE, SMALLEST FIX in this bucket. use-of-color-v0.md:58-60 instructs: 'When the handed axe link-in-text-block signal reports PASS, DEFER to it — axe measured exactly this link-vs-surrounding-text separation.' That clause can never fire: act-page-collect.js:1100 runs axe with `resultTypes: ['violations','incomplete']`, so passes are never collected, and axe-surface.js:156-157 only emits from collect.axe and collect.axeIncomplete. I ran axe directly on all three link pages: link-in-text-block PASSES every link on every one of them (case-06 4/4, case-07 4/4, case-04 5/5), with the check message 'Links can be distinguished from surrounding text in some way other than by color'. Had the pass been plumbed, all three FPs would have cleared. Note this is a POSITIVE measurement, not an absence — it does not violate the 'absence != pass' invariant, which is exactly the distinction the rubric already draws.
patterns.proposedFix: act-page-collect.js:1100 — add 'passes' to resultTypes and map them alongside violations/incomplete; axe-surface.js — emit allow-listed rule passes as kind:'pass' (review:false); llm-adjudicator.js — surface them as a `checkerCleared` signal on the subject. Scope the deference to MEASURING rules on the allow-list (link-in-text-block), not to bare rule-did-not-fire. Gate on the 1.4.1 FN slice before shipping.

patterns.name: Judge fabricates numeric contrast/luminance ratios instead of measuring
patterns.description: The rubric asks for a numeric >=3:1 link-vs-prose luminance judgment from a crop, with no deterministic value handed over and no tool called. Result: on case-06 the SAME judge in the SAME run gave '3.91:1' (correct) to one link and '2.87:1' (fabricated; true value 3.913) to another link in the SAME paragraph with byte-identical computed style. On case-07 two of three barrier summaries cite colours (#2563eb/#374151, #555555) that appear nowhere in the page's CSS. On case-04 four identically-styled links got four different rationales, two of them asserting an underline that computed style says is `none`. The verdicts are not tracking any measurement.
patterns.proposedFix: Hand the judge the deterministic computed link colour, prose colour and precomputed WCAG ratio (the collector already computes contrast signals), the way enclosingContext is handed for 2.4.4 — and forbid the judge from asserting a ratio it was not given. Combine with the axe-pass plumbing above.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 1 case beyond the two already counted above (case-06); the other two are double-counted with the applicability pattern

patterns.name: Judge overrides the deterministic signal it was told is authoritative
patterns.description: Two different rubrics, same shape: the rubric states the correct rule, hands the judge the correct evidence, and the judge decides against both. In 2.4.4 the collector supplied enclosingBlockText naming the destination ('...for full pricing details') and link-purpose-v0.md:42-45 mandates NOT REPRODUCED for that exact condition; the judge's own summary concedes the enclosing context describes the destination and flags anyway, treating 'click here' as a per-se failure (G53 is a sufficient technique that says otherwise). In 2.4.3 focus-order-meaning-v0.md forbids flagging on visual-order mismatch twice (:23-25 and :43-45); the judge's entire stated basis is 'inverting the logical left-to-right reading order visible on screen', with no impaired task named.
patterns.proposedFix: Make the authoritative-signal deference structural rather than prose: require the JSON output to carry the deterministic field it relied on (e.g. `blockTextUsed`, `impairedTask`) and reject a REPRODUCED verdict that contradicts the handed signal or leaves the required field empty. Add worked PASS examples for both shapes ('click here' + enclosing sentence; two independent columns reordered by flex `order`).
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 2 cases

patterns.name: Rubrics are asymmetric: a hard 'absence is not a pass' invariant with only soft counterweights
patterns.description: Cross-cutting, and it explains WHY the FPs concentrate on control/boundary pages. Every rubric carries the same all-caps hard invariant ('CRITICAL invariant: ABSENCE OF A DETERMINISTIC FINDING IS NOT A PASS') plus barrier-hunting framing ('hunt for the second cue', 'if no non-color cue is visible where one is needed, that is the barrier'), while the counterweights are soft prose ('WCAG soundness caveats: do NOT manufacture a failure these don't support'). On a page deliberately built to sit ON the pass/fail line, the hard rule wins over the soft caveat. 11 of the 14 FP pages self-describe in their scenario metadata as a boundary / control / escape-hatch / near-PASS variant.
patterns.proposedFix: Add a symmetric hard invariant: 'A verified, specific conforming cue IS a pass. Before returning REPRODUCED you must name the specific cue you looked for, the measurement you made, and where you looked — a verdict with no cited measurement is PARTIAL, not a barrier.' Pair it with the structural output fields above so it is enforceable rather than exhortative.
patterns.estimatedRecovery: 0 additional (overlaps the patterns above); this is the framing fix that keeps them from recurring
